title.zh: 卷48 列傳第40 蕭詧
title.raw: 卷48 列傳第40 蕭詧 Volume 48 Biographies 40: Xiao Cha

sentences.zh: 蕭詧字理孫，蘭陵人也，梁武帝之孫，昭明太子統之第三子。

translations.literal: Xiao Cha, courtesy name Lisun, was a native of Lanling. He was a grandson of Emperor Wu of Liang and the third son of Crown Prince Zhaoming, Xiao Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha, whose courtesy name was Lisun, came from Lanling. He was a grandson of Emperor Wu of Liang and the third son of Crown Prince Zhaoming, Xiao Tong.

sentences.zh: 幼而好學，善屬文，尤長佛義。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, and especially excelled in Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: He had loved learning since childhood, was adept at prose composition, and was especially accomplished in Buddhist teachings.

sentences.zh: 特為梁武帝所嘉賞。

translations.literal: He was especially praised and favored by Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang held him in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 梁普通六年，封曲江縣公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong of Liang, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Putong era (525), he was created Duke of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，進封岳陽郡王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong, he was advanced to Prince of Yueyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongdatong (531), he was promoted to Prince of Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 歷官宣惠將軍，知石頭戍事，琅邪、彭城二郡太守，東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of General Who Proclaims Grace, supervised the garrison affairs at Shitou, served as governor of the two commanderies of Langye and Pengcheng, and was Regional Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In succession he served as General Who Proclaims Grace, supervised the Shitou garrison, governed both Langye and Pengcheng commanderies, and held the post of regional inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，昭明卒，梁武帝舍詧兄弟而立簡文，內常愧之，寵亞諸子，以會稽人物殷阜，一都之會，故有此授，以慰其心。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhaoming died, Emperor Wu of Liang passed over Cha and his brothers and established Jianwen as heir. He always felt inwardly guilty about this and favored Cha nearly as much as his own sons. Because Kuaiji was rich in distinguished men and was the metropolis of a whole commandery, he made this appointment to console Cha's heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, Emperor Wu had passed over Cha and his brothers in favor of establishing Jianwen as heir, a decision that weighed on him. He lavished favor on Cha nearly equal to his own sons. As Kuaiji boasted a wealthy population of talented men and stood as the chief city of its region, he granted Cha this post to soothe his feelings.

sentences.zh: 詧旣以其昆弟不得為嗣，常懷不平。

translations.literal: Since Cha and his brothers had not been made heirs, he constantly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Because he and his brothers had been passed over for succession, Cha nursed a lasting grievance.

sentences.zh: 又以梁武帝衰老，朝多秕政，有敗亡之漸，遂蓄聚貨財，交通賓客，招募輕俠，折節下之。

translations.literal: Moreover, seeing that Emperor Wu of Liang was aged and that the court had many corrupt policies with signs of impending collapse, he began to amass wealth, cultivate ties with guests, recruit daredevils, and humble himself before them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor grow old and the court mired in misgovernment with collapse on the horizon, he began stockpiling wealth, cultivating guests, and recruiting bold spirits, to whom he showed deliberate deference.

sentences.zh: 其勇敢者多歸附，左右遂至數千人，皆厚加資給。

translations.literal: Many of the brave came to attach themselves to him, and those around him soon reached several thousand men, all generously provided for.
translations.idiomatic: The bold flocked to his side until his entourage numbered in the thousands, all handsomely maintained at his expense.

sentences.zh: 昔之善為政者，不獨師所見。

translations.literal: Those in former times who governed well did not rely solely on what they themselves had seen.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers of old who governed well did not learn only from their own experience.

sentences.zh: 藉聽衆賢，則所聞自遠；

translations.literal: If they borrowed the hearing of many worthies, what they learned reached far indeed;
translations.idiomatic: By heeding many worthy advisers, they heard reports from far and wide;

sentences.zh: 資鑒外物，故在矚致明。

translations.literal: They took external things as mirrors, and thus in their oversight achieved clarity.
translations.idiomatic: they used the world beyond themselves as a mirror, and so saw clearly in all they surveyed.

sentences.zh: 是以龐參恤民，蓋訪言於高逸；

translations.literal: Therefore Pang Can cared for the people—he sought counsel from lofty recluses;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Pang Can, in caring for the people, sought out the words of lofty recluses;

sentences.zh: 馬援居政，每責成於掾史；

translations.literal: Ma Yuan in administering affairs daily held his clerks accountable;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan in office constantly demanded results from his staff;

sentences.zh: 王沉爰加厚賞；

translations.literal: Wang Chen accordingly bestowed generous rewards;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen for his part heaped rewards upon the worthy;

sentences.zh: 呂虔功有所由：故能顯美政於當年，流芳塵於後代。

translations.literal: Lü Qian had a source for his achievements: thus they were able to display fine governance in their own day and leave a fragrant name for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: and Lü Qian owed his achievements to such means—each manifesting good government in his own time and leaving a lasting reputation for posterity.

sentences.zh: 吾以陋識，來牧盛藩。

translations.literal: With my shallow understanding I have come to govern this great territory.
translations.idiomatic: With my limited understanding I have come to govern this great principality.

sentences.zh: 每慮德不被民，政道或紊。

translations.literal: I constantly worry that my virtue does not reach the people and that governance may fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I worry constantly that my virtue does not reach the people and that policy may fall into disarray.

sentences.zh: 中宵拊枕，對案忘饑，思納良謨，以匡弗逮。

translations.literal: At midnight I beat my pillow; facing my desk I forget hunger, thinking to adopt good counsel to remedy my inadequacies.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight I strike my pillow in frustration; I sit before my desk forgetful of hunger, seeking sound counsel to remedy what I lack.

sentences.zh: 雍州部內有不便於民，不利於政，長吏貪殘，戍將懦弱，關市恣其裒刻，豪猾多所苞藏，並密以名聞，當加厘正。

translations.literal: Within Yongzhou there are matters inconvenient to the people and harmful to governance—district chiefs who are greedy and cruel, garrison commanders who are weak and timid, market tolls levied without restraint, and powerful scoundrels who shelter much wrongdoing. Report all these in secret by name, and they shall be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: If anything within Yongzhou harms the people or hinders good government—corrupt district officials, cowardly garrison commanders, extortion at the markets, or powerful ruffians who shield wrongdoing—report it all to me in confidence by name, and it will be set right.

sentences.zh: 若刺史治道之要，弛張未允，循酷乖理，任用違才，或愛狎邪佞，或斥廢忠謇，彌思啟告，用袪未悟。

translations.literal: If in the essentials of the regional inspector's governance the tight and loose are not properly balanced, lenience and severity run counter to reason, appointments fail to match talent, or he dotes on wicked flatterers while dismissing loyal and forthright men, think all the more to inform me, so that my blindness may be removed.
translations.idiomatic: If I myself, as regional inspector, fail to balance severity and lenience, appoint the wrong men, favor wicked flatterers, or cast aside loyal and honest advisers, tell me all the more plainly, so that I may be awakened from my errors.

sentences.zh: 鹽梅舟烜，允屬良規，苦口惡石，想勿余隱。

translations.literal: Salt and plum, boat and helm—these properly belong to good counsel; bitter words and harsh medicine—I trust you will not hold anything back from me.
translations.idiomatic: You are the seasoning for the state and the helm for its vessel—such counsel is what I need. Though your words be bitter as medicine, I trust you will withhold nothing.

sentences.zh: 並廣示鄉閭，知其款意。

translations.literal: All this is to be broadly displayed in villages and neighborhoods so that people may know my sincere intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be posted widely throughout the countryside so that all may know my earnest intent.

sentences.zh: 於是境內稱治。

translations.literal: Thereupon the territory within the borders was said to be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: On this account the realm within his borders was praised as well governed.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，梁武帝以詧兄河東王譽為湘州刺史，徙湘州刺史張纘為雍州以代詧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Emperor Wu of Liang appointed Cha's elder brother, Prince of Hedong Xiao Yu, as Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou, and transferred the Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou, Zhang Zuan, to Yongzhou to replace Cha.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing (548), Emperor Wu appointed Cha's elder brother, Prince of Hedong Xiao Yu, regional inspector of Xiangzhou, and moved Zhang Zuan from Xiangzhou to Yongzhou to replace Cha.

sentences.zh: 纘恃其才望，志氣矜驕，輕譽少年，州府迎候有闕。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan relied on his talent and reputation; his spirit was proud and arrogant, and he looked down on the young Yu. The prefectural and commandery offices were deficient in their reception and attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan, confident in his talent and standing, carried himself with arrogant pride and treated the young Yu with contempt. The prefectural and commandery offices failed to receive him with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 譽深銜之。

translations.literal: Yu deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu bore a deep grudge over the slight.

sentences.zh: 及至鎮，遂託疾不與纘相見。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zuan reached his post, Yu feigned illness and refused to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Zuan had taken up his post, Yu pleaded illness and refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 後聞侯景作亂，頗淩蹙纘。

translations.literal: Later, when he heard that Hou Jing had risen in rebellion, he greatly pressed and harassed Zhang Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when news came that Hou Jing had rebelled, he pressed Zhang Zuan hard.

sentences.zh: 纘懼為所擒，乃輕舟夜遁，將之雍部，復慮詧拒之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan feared being seized by him, so he fled by light boat in the night, intending to go to the Yong region, but again worried that Cha would refuse him entry.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capture, Zhang Zuan slipped away by light boat in the night, heading for Yong province—but he worried that Cha would bar his way.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝時鎮江陵，與纘有舊，纘將因之以斃詧兄弟。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang was then stationed at Jiangling and had old ties with Zhang Zuan; Zhang Zuan intended to rely on him to destroy Cha and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang was then based at Jiangling and was an old associate of Zhang Zuan's; Zhang Zuan planned to use him to destroy Cha and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 會梁元帝與譽及信州刺史、桂陽王慥各率所領，入援金陵。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Yuan of Liang, together with Yu and the Regional Inspector of Xinzhou, Prince of Guiyang Xiao Kai, each led their forces to enter Jinling in relief.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yuan, Yu, and Xiao Kai, prince of Guiyang and regional inspector of Xinzhou, each led their troops to relieve Jinling.

sentences.zh: 慥下峽至江津，譽次江口，梁元帝屆郢州之武成。

translations.literal: Kai descended the gorge to Jiangjin; Yu halted at the river mouth; Emperor Yuan of Liang arrived at Wucheng in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kai came down the gorge to Jiangjin, Yu encamped at the river mouth, and Emperor Yuan reached Wucheng in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景已請和，梁武帝詔罷援軍。

translations.literal: Just then Hou Jing had already sued for peace, and Emperor Wu of Liang ordered the relief armies disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hou Jing had already sued for peace, and Emperor Wu ordered the relief armies withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 譽自江口將旋湘鎮，慥欲待梁元帝至，謁督府，方還州。

translations.literal: Yu was about to return from the river mouth to his post in Xiang, while Kai wished to wait until Emperor Yuan of Liang arrived, pay his respects at the headquarters, and only then return to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was preparing to return from the river mouth to his post in Xiang, while Kai wanted to wait for Emperor Yuan, pay his respects at headquarters, and only then go home to his province.

sentences.zh: 纘時在江陵，乃貽梁元帝書曰：「河東戴檣上水，欲襲江陵。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan was then at Jiangling and sent a letter to Emperor Yuan of Liang saying: "The Prince of Hedong has raised sails and is coming upstream, intending to attack Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan was then at Jiangling and wrote to Emperor Yuan: "The Prince of Hedong has raised sail and is coming upstream to strike at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 岳陽在雍，共謀不逞。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Yueyang is in Yong and shares in the plot, which has not yet succeeded."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yueyang holds Yong and is their co-conspirator, though the plot has not yet succeeded."

sentences.zh: 江陵游軍主朱榮又遣使報云：「桂陽住此，卻應譽、詧。」

translations.literal: The roaming-army commander of Jiangling, Zhu Rong, also sent a messenger reporting: "The Prince of Guiyang is staying here but is in fact responding to Yu and Cha."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rong, commander of the roaming forces at Jiangling, also sent word: "The Prince of Guiyang is lingering here but is really in league with Yu and Cha."

sentences.zh: 梁元帝信之，乃鑿船沉米，斬纜而歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang believed this, whereupon he bored holes in the boats and sank the grain, cut the mooring cables, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan believed them, bored holes in his boats, sank his grain stores, cut his mooring lines, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 至江陵，收慥殺之。

translations.literal: When he reached Jiangling, he seized Kai and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Jiangling he seized Kai and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 令其子方等、王僧辯等相繼攻譽於湘州。

translations.literal: He ordered his son Fangdeng, Wang Sengbian, and others in succession to attack Yu in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Fangdeng, Wang Sengbian, and others in turn to attack Yu in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 譽又告急於詧。

translations.literal: Yu again sent an urgent appeal to Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Yu again sent an urgent appeal for help to Cha.

sentences.zh: 詧聞之大怒。

translations.literal: When Cha heard of this, he was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was furious when he heard of it.

sentences.zh: 初，梁元帝將援建業，令所督諸州，竝發兵下赴國難。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was about to relieve Jianye, he ordered all the provinces under his supervision to send troops downstream together to meet the national crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Yuan was preparing to relieve Jianye, he had ordered all the provinces under his command to march downstream to the empire's aid.

sentences.zh: 詧遣府司馬劉方貴領兵為前軍，出漢口。

translations.literal: Cha sent his prefectural marshal Liu Fanggui to lead troops as the vanguard, setting out from Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Cha sent his prefectural marshal Liu Fanggui at the head of the vanguard, marching out from Hankou.

sentences.zh: 及將發，元帝又使諮議參軍劉鈺喻詧，令自行。

translations.literal: Just as they were about to depart, Emperor Yuan again sent Advisory Aide Liu Yu to instruct Cha to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Just before they were to march, Emperor Yuan sent advisory aide Liu Yu to tell Cha he must go in person.

sentences.zh: 詧辭頗不順，元帝又怒。

translations.literal: Cha's reply was rather disobliging, and Emperor Yuan grew angry again.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's reply was distinctly uncooperative, and Emperor Yuan was angered anew.

sentences.zh: 而方貴先與詧不協，潛與元帝相知，剋期襲詧。

translations.literal: Fanggui had long been at odds with Cha and secretly kept in contact with Emperor Yuan, setting a date to attack Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Fanggui had long been on bad terms with Cha and was secretly in league with Emperor Yuan, with a fixed date set to strike at Cha.

sentences.zh: 未及發，會詧以他事召方貴，方貴疑謀泄，遂據樊城拒命。

translations.literal: Before they could act, Cha summoned Fanggui on another matter; Fanggui suspected the plot had leaked and thereupon seized Fancheng and defied orders.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could strike, Cha summoned Fanggui on another matter; fearing exposure, Fanggui seized Fancheng and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詧遣使魏益德、杜岸等衆軍攻之。

translations.literal: Cha sent Wei Yide, Du An, and the rest of the army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha sent Wei Yide, Du An, and the combined forces to attack him.

sentences.zh: 方貴窘急，令其子遷超乞師於江陵。

translations.literal: Fanggui, hard pressed, sent his son Qianchao to beg for troops at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, Fanggui sent his son Qianchao to Jiangling to beg for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 元帝乃厚資遣纘，若將述職，而密援方貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan then richly equipped and sent off Zhang Zuan as if he were going to assume his post, while secretly aiding Fanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan then sent Zhang Zuan off with lavish supplies, as though he were simply taking up his post, while secretly supporting Fanggui.

sentences.zh: 纘次大堤，樊城已陷。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan halted at Dadi, but Fancheng had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan halted at Dadi, but Fancheng had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 詧擒方貴兄弟及黨與，竝斬之。

translations.literal: Cha captured Fanggui, his brothers, and their associates, and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cha captured Fanggui, his brothers, and their followers and beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 纘因進至州。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan thereupon advanced to the provincial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan thereupon advanced to the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 詧遷延不受代，乃以西城居之，待之以禮。

translations.literal: Cha delayed and would not accept the transfer of office; he had Zhang Zuan lodge in the western city and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Cha stalled and refused to hand over power; he lodged Zhang Zuan in the western quarter of the city and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 軍民之政，猶歸於詧。

translations.literal: Military and civil administration still remained with Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Military and civil affairs still remained in Cha's hands.

sentences.zh: 詧以構其兄弟，事始於纘，將密圖之。

translations.literal: Cha held that the plot against his brothers had begun with Zhang Zuan and was about to scheme secretly against him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha blamed Zhang Zuan for having set the plot against his brothers in motion and was planning to deal with him in secret.

sentences.zh: 纘懼，請元帝召之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan was afraid and asked Emperor Yuan to summon him away.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhang Zuan asked Emperor Yuan to recall him.

sentences.zh: 元帝乃征纘於詧，詧留不遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan thereupon ordered Cha to send Zhang Zuan back, but Cha detained him and would not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan ordered Cha to send Zhang Zuan back, but Cha detained him and refused to let him go.

sentences.zh: 杜岸兄弟紿纘曰：「民觀岳陽殿下，勢不仰容。

translations.literal: The brothers Du An deceived Zhang Zuan, saying: "We observe that His Highness the Prince of Yueyang will by no means submit to your authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Du brothers deceived Zhang Zuan, saying: "We can see that the Prince of Yueyang will never bow to your authority.

sentences.zh: 不如且往西山，以避此禍。

translations.literal: It would be better for now to go to the Western Hills to escape this disaster.
translations.idiomatic: You would do better to withdraw to the Western Hills for now and escape this danger.

sentences.zh: 使君旣得物情，遠近必當歸集，以此義舉，事無不濟。」

translations.literal: Once you, my lord, have won the hearts of the people, those near and far will surely rally to you; with this righteous undertaking, nothing will fail."
translations.idiomatic: Once you have won popular support, men near and far will surely rally to you; with such a righteous cause, you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 纘深以為然，因與岸等結盟誓。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan was deeply convinced and thereupon formed a sworn alliance with An and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan was thoroughly persuaded and formed a sworn alliance with An and the others.

sentences.zh: 纘又要雍州人席引等於西山聚衆。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan also enlisted the Yongzhou men Xi Yin and others to gather a force on the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan also enlisted Xi Yin of Yongzhou and others to raise a force on the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 纘乃服婦人衣，乘青布轝，與親信十餘人出奔。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan then put on women's clothing, rode in a blue-cloth palanquin, and fled with a dozen or so trusted followers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan disguised himself in women's clothing, rode in a blue-cloth palanquin, and fled with a dozen trusted followers.

sentences.zh: 引等與杜岸馳告詧。

translations.literal: Yin and the others, together with Du An, galloped to inform Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and the others, together with Du An, galloped off to inform Cha.

sentences.zh: 詧令中兵參軍尹正共岸等率兵追討，竝擒之。

translations.literal: Cha ordered Central Troops Aide Yin Zheng, together with An and the others, to lead troops in pursuit and capture them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cha ordered central troops aide Yin Zheng, together with An and the others, to pursue them and took them all captive.

sentences.zh: 纘懼不免，因請為沙門。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan, fearing he could not escape death, thereupon asked to become a Buddhist monk.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, Zhang Zuan asked to be ordained as a Buddhist monk.

sentences.zh: 詧時以譽危急，乃留諮議參軍蔡大寶守襄陽，率衆二萬、騎千匹伐江陵以救之。

translations.literal: At that time Yu was in grave danger, so Cha left Advisory Aide Cai Dabao to guard Xiangyang and led twenty thousand infantry and a thousand horsemen to attack Jiangling in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was then in grave danger, so Cha left advisory aide Cai Dabao to guard Xiangyang and marched on Jiangling with twenty thousand foot soldiers and a thousand cavalry to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 于時江陵立柵，周遶郭邑，而北面未就。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangling had erected palisades encircling the walled city, but the northern side was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling had by then thrown up palisades around the city walls, but the northern side was not yet finished.

sentences.zh: 詧因攻之。

translations.literal: Cha thereupon attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Cha attacked there.

sentences.zh: 元帝大懼，乃遣參軍庾奐謂詧曰：「正德肆亂，天下崩離。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was greatly afraid and sent Aide Yu Huan to say to Cha: "Zhengde ran riot and the realm split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was terrified and sent aide Yu Huan to tell Cha: "When Zhengde ran riot the empire split apart.

sentences.zh: 汝復效尤，將欲何謂？

translations.literal: You now follow his example—what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: You now follow his example—what do you mean by it?

sentences.zh: 吾蒙先

translations.literal: I received the former
translations.idiomatic: I received the former

translations.literal: (emperor's)
translations.idiomatic: (emperor's)

sentences.zh: 〔宮〕愛顧，以汝兄弟見屬。

translations.literal: [en] loving regard, and you brothers were entrusted to me.
translations.idiomatic: emperor's gracious favor, and your brothers were placed in my charge.

sentences.zh: 今以侄伐叔，逆順安在？」

translations.literal: Now you as nephew attack your uncle—where is the right order in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you as nephew attack your uncle—where is right and wrong in that?"

sentences.zh: 詧謂奐曰：「家兄無罪，累被攻圍。

translations.literal: Cha said to Huan: "My elder brother is innocent, yet he has repeatedly been besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Cha told Huan: "My elder brother is innocent, yet he has been besieged again and again.

sentences.zh: 同氣之情，豈可坐觀成敗。

translations.literal: The bond of shared blood—how could I sit by and watch the outcome?
translations.idiomatic: How could I, sharing the same blood, sit idle and watch his fate?

sentences.zh: 七父若顧先恩，豈應若是。

translations.literal: If my seventh uncle still cared for our former sovereign's grace, how could he act as he does?
translations.idiomatic: If you, my seventh uncle, still honored our former sovereign's grace, how could you act as you do?

sentences.zh: 如能退兵湘水，吾便旋旆襄陽。」

translations.literal: If you can withdraw your troops to the Xiang River, I will turn my banners back to Xiangyang."
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw your troops to the Xiang River, and I will turn back to Xiangyang."

sentences.zh: 詧旣攻柵不克，退而築城。

translations.literal: Cha, having failed to take the palisades, withdrew and built a fortified camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha failed to breach the palisades, he withdrew and built a fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 又盡銳攻之。

translations.literal: He again attacked with all his elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked again with his best troops.

sentences.zh: 會大雨暴至，平地水四尺，詧軍中沾漬，衆頗離心。

translations.literal: Just then a violent rainstorm burst upon them; on level ground the water stood four feet deep. Cha's army was soaked through, and the troops grew quite disaffected.
translations.idiomatic: A violent rainstorm struck; on level ground the water stood four feet deep. Cha's army was drenched, and his men began to lose heart.

sentences.zh: 其將杜岸、岸弟幼安及其兄子龕，懼詧不振，以其屬降於江陵。

translations.literal: His generals Du An, An's younger brother You'an, and their elder brother's son Kan, fearing that Cha would not recover, surrendered their followers to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Du An, An's younger brother You'an, and their nephew Kan, fearing Cha would not prevail, surrendered their men to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 詧衆大駭，其夜遁歸襄陽，器械輜重，多沒於湕水。

translations.literal: Cha's army was greatly alarmed; that night they fled back to Xiangyang, and much of their weapons and baggage train was lost in the Xun River.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's army panicked; that night they fled back to Xiangyang, and much of their arms and baggage was lost in the Xun River.

sentences.zh: 初，詧囚張纘於軍，至是，先殺纘而後退焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Cha had held Zhang Zuan prisoner in the army; on this occasion he killed Zhang Zuan first and only then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had kept Zhang Zuan prisoner in his camp; now he killed Zhang Zuan before retreating.

sentences.zh: 杜岸之降也，請以五百騎襲襄陽。

translations.literal: When Du An surrendered, he asked to lead five hundred horsemen in a surprise attack on Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Du An surrendered, he asked permission to lead five hundred cavalry in a surprise raid on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 去城三十里，城中覺之。

translations.literal: When they were thirty li from the city, those inside detected them.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from the city, the garrison detected them.

sentences.zh: 蔡大寶乃輔詧母保林龔氏，登陴閉門拒戰。

translations.literal: Cai Dabao thereupon assisted Cha's mother, the Lady of Baolin of the Gong clan, to ascend the walls, shut the gates, and resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Dabao helped Cha's mother, Lady Gong of Baolin, mount the walls, shut the gates, and hold the city.

sentences.zh: 會詧夜至，龔氏不知其敗，謂為賊也，至曉見詧，乃納之。

translations.literal: It happened that Cha arrived in the night; Lady Gong did not know of his defeat and took him for the enemy. At dawn, when she saw it was Cha, she admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha arrived that night; Lady Gong, unaware of his defeat, took him for the enemy. At dawn, seeing it was Cha, she let him in.

sentences.zh: 岸等以詧至，遂奔其兄巘於廣平。

translations.literal: An and the others, seeing that Cha had arrived, thereupon fled to his elder brother Yan at Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When An and his men learned Cha had returned, they fled to his elder brother Yan at Guangping.

sentences.zh: 詧遣將尹正、薛暉等攻拔之，獲巘、岸等，竝其母妻子女，並於襄陽北門殺之。

translations.literal: Cha sent his generals Yin Zheng, Xue Hui, and others to attack and take them, capturing Yan, An, and the rest together with their mothers, wives, sons, and daughters, and beheaded them all at the north gate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cha sent Yin Zheng, Xue Hui, and others to attack and capture them, taking Yan, An, and the rest together with their mothers, wives, sons, and daughters, and executed them all at the north gate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 盡誅諸杜宗族親者，其幼稚疏屬下蠶室。

translations.literal: He executed to the last all members of the Du clan and their kin; the young and distant relations were sent to the silkworm chambers.
translations.idiomatic: He put to death every member of the Du clan and their kin; the young and more distant relations were castrated and sent to the silkworm chambers.

sentences.zh: 又發掘其墳墓，燒其骸骨，灰而揚之。

translations.literal: He also exhumed their graves, burned their bones, and scattered the ashes to the winds.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug up their graves, burned their bones, and scattered the ashes to the winds.

sentences.zh: 詧旣與江陵構隙，恐不能自固，大統十五年，乃遣使稱藩，請為附庸。

translations.literal: Cha, having fallen out with Jiangling and fearing he could not hold his own, in the fifteenth year of Datong sent envoys to declare himself a vassal and ask to become a dependent state.
translations.idiomatic: Having broken with Jiangling and fearing he could not hold out alone, in the fifteenth year of Datong (549) Cha sent envoys to submit as a vassal and ask to become a Zhou dependency.

sentences.zh: 太祖令丞相府東合祭酒榮權使焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor ordered Rong Quan, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion in the Chancellor's Office, to go as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Yuwen Tai sent Rong Quan, libationer of the Eastern Pavilion in the chancellor's office, as his envoy.

sentences.zh: 詧大悅。

translations.literal: Cha was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，梁元帝令柳仲禮率衆進圖襄陽。

translations.literal: That year, Emperor Yuan of Liang ordered Liu Zhongli to lead his forces forward to besiege Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Emperor Yuan of Liang ordered Liu Zhongli to lead an army against Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 詧懼，乃遣其妻王氏及世子嶚為質以請救。

translations.literal: Cha was afraid and sent his wife Lady Wang and his heir apparent Kui as hostages to request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Xiao Cha sent his wife Lady Wang and his heir apparent Kui as hostages to plead for aid.

sentences.zh: 太祖又令榮權報命，仍遣開府楊忠率兵援之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor also ordered Rong Quan to return with a reply and further sent Grand General Yang Zhong to lead troops to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Yuwen Tai also sent Rong Quan back with a reply and dispatched Grand General Yang Zhong with an army to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，楊忠擒仲禮，平漢東，詧乃獲安。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Yang Zhong captured Zhongli, pacified Handong, and Cha then obtained safety.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Yang Zhong captured Liu Zhongli and pacified Handong, and Xiao Cha was at last secure.

sentences.zh: 時朝議欲令詧發喪嗣位，詧以未有璽命，辭不敢當。

translations.literal: At the time the court deliberated on having Cha observe mourning and succeed to the throne; Cha, because he had not yet received an imperial seal decree, declined and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated having Xiao Cha declare mourning and take the throne, but he declined, saying that without an imperial seal decree he did not dare assume the position.

sentences.zh: 榮權時在詧所，乃馳還，具言其狀。

translations.literal: Rong Quan was then at Cha's residence; he galloped back and reported the situation in full.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Quan was then with Xiao Cha; he rode back at once and reported the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂令假散騎常侍鄭穆及榮權持節策命詧為梁王。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor then ordered Acting Supervising Cavalry Regular Attendant Zheng Mu and Rong Quan to bear credentials and invest Cha as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor then sent Acting Supervising Cavalry Regular Attendant Zheng Mu and Rong Quan with credentials to invest Xiao Cha as King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 詧乃於襄陽置百官，承制封拜。

translations.literal: Cha then established the full bureaucracy at Xiangyang and enfeoffed and appointed officials under delegated imperial authority.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha then established a full bureaucracy at Xiangyang and issued enfeoffments and appointments under delegated imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詧留蔡大寶居守，乃自襄陽來朝。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Cha left Cai Dabao to hold the city and came from Xiangyang to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Xiao Cha left Cai Dabao to guard Xiangyang and came to court in person.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂詧曰：「王之來此，頗由榮權，王欲見之乎？」

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor said to Cha: "Your coming here owes much to Rong Quan; would you like to see him?"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor said to Xiao Cha, "Your coming here owes a great deal to Rong Quan. Would you like to meet him?"

sentences.zh: 詧曰：「幸甚。」

translations.literal: Cha said: "I would be most fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha said, "I would be most honored."

sentences.zh: 太祖乃召權與詧相見。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor then summoned Quan to meet with Cha.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor then summoned Rong Quan to meet with Xiao Cha.

sentences.zh: 仍謂之曰：「榮權，起士也，寡人與之從事，未嘗見其失信。」

translations.literal: He again said to him: "Rong Quan is a man risen from common stock; I have worked with him and never seen him break his word."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Rong Quan is a self-made man. I have worked with him and never known him to break his word."

sentences.zh: 詧曰：「榮常侍通二國之言無私，故詧今者得歸誠魏闕耳。」

translations.literal: Cha said: "Attendant Rong conveyed the words between our two states without partiality; that is why I am now able to come in loyalty to the Wei court."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha said, "Attendant Rong conveyed messages between our two states without favoritism. That is why I am now able to offer my loyalty at the Wei court."

sentences.zh: 初，江陵滅，梁元帝將王琳據湘州，志圖匡復。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiangling fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang's general Wang Lin held Xiang Province and set his mind on restoring the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the fall of Jiangling, Emperor Yuan of Liang's general Wang Lin held Xiang Province and hoped to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及詧立，琳乃遣其將潘純陀、侯方兒來寇。

translations.literal: When Cha was established, Lin then sent his generals Pan Chuntuo and Hou Fang'er to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiao Cha was established as king, Wang Lin sent his generals Pan Chuntuo and Hou Fang'er to attack him.

sentences.zh: 詧出師禦之，純陀等退歸夏口。

translations.literal: Cha marched out to repel them, and Chuntuo and the others withdrew to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha marched out to meet them, and Chuntuo and his men retreated to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 詧之四年，詧遣其大將軍王操率兵畧取王琳之長沙、武陵、南平等郡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cha's reign, Cha sent his Grand General Wang Cao to lead troops in seizing Wang Lin's commanderies of Changsha, Wuling, and Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of his reign, Xiao Cha sent his Grand General Wang Cao to seize Changsha, Wuling, Nanping, and other commanderies from Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 五年，王琳又遣其將雷又柔襲陷監利郡，太守蔡大有死之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Wang Lin again sent his general Lei Yourou to raid and capture Jianli Commandery; the prefect Cai Dayou died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Wang Lin sent his general Lei Yourou to raid and capture Jianli Commandery, and Prefect Cai Dayou was killed.

sentences.zh: 尋而琳與陳人相持，稱藩乞師於詧。

translations.literal: Before long Lin was locked in stalemate with the Chen forces; he declared himself a vassal and requested troops from Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Lin was locked in stalemate with Chen forces and, declaring himself a vassal, asked Xiao Cha for military aid.

sentences.zh: 詧許之。

translations.literal: Cha agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha agreed.

sentences.zh: 師未出而琳軍敗，附於齊。

translations.literal: Before the army marched out, Lin's forces were defeated and he submitted to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Before the relief army could march, Wang Lin's forces were defeated and he submitted to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，其太子巋來朝京師。

translations.literal: That year, his crown prince Kui came to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year, his crown prince Kui came to the capital on a court visit.

sentences.zh: 詧之六年夏，震，其前殿崩，壓殺二百餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Cha's reign, summer, there was an earthquake; the front hall collapsed and crushed more than two hundred people to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of his reign, during summer, an earthquake struck; the front hall collapsed and killed more than two hundred people.

sentences.zh: 初，江陵平，詧將尹德毅說詧曰：「臣聞人主之行，與匹夫不同。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jiangling was pacified, Cha's general Yin Deyi urged Cha, saying: "I have heard that a ruler's conduct differs from that of a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Jiangling was taken, Xiao Cha's general Yin Deyi urged him, saying, "I have heard that a ruler's conduct is not the same as a common man's.

sentences.zh: 匹夫者，飾小行，競小廉，以取名譽。

translations.literal: A common man polishes small deeds and competes in petty integrity to win reputation.
translations.idiomatic: A common man polishes small deeds and vies in petty scruples to win a name.

sentences.zh: 人主者，定天下，安社稷，以成大功。

translations.literal: A ruler settles the realm, secures the altars of state, and achieves great merit.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler settles the realm, secures the altars of state, and achieves great things.

sentences.zh: 今魏虜貪惏，罔顧弔民伐罪之義，必欲肆其殘忍，多所誅夷，俘囚士庶，並為軍實。

translations.literal: Now the Wei invaders are greedy and cruel; they heed not the principle of comforting the people and punishing the guilty. They are sure to indulge their brutality, executing many, capturing scholars and commoners—all made into military booty.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Wei invaders are greedy and cruel. They ignore the principle of comforting the people and punishing the guilty, and are sure to indulge their brutality—executing many, capturing scholars and commoners, and turning them all into military booty.

sentences.zh: 然此等戚屬，咸在江東，念其充餌豺狼，見拘異域，痛心疾首，何日能忘！

translations.literal: Yet these kinsmen are all in Jiangdong; thinking how they serve as fodder for wolves and jackals, held captive in foreign lands—heartbroken, head aching—what day can this be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: Yet these kinsmen are all in Jiangdong. To think of them as fodder for wolves and jackals, held captive in a foreign land—my heart breaks and my head aches. What day can I forget this!

sentences.zh: 殿下方清宇宙，紹茲鴻緒。

translations.literal: Your Highness is now pacifying the universe and inheriting this great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is now pacifying the realm and inheriting this great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 悠悠之人，不可門到戶說。

translations.literal: The common multitudes cannot be persuaded by going door to door.
translations.idiomatic: The common people cannot be won over by going from door to door.

sentences.zh: 其塗炭至此，咸謂殿下為之。

translations.literal: That they suffer such char and flood, all say Your Highness is responsible.
translations.idiomatic: That they suffer such ruin, everyone says Your Highness is to blame.

sentences.zh: 殿下旣殺人父兄，孤人子弟，人盡讎也，誰與為國。

translations.literal: Your Highness has slain men's fathers and elder brothers and left sons and younger brothers orphaned—all bear grievances; with whom will you build the state?
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has killed men's fathers and elder brothers and left sons and younger brothers orphaned. Everyone bears a grudge—who will serve the state with you?

sentences.zh: 但魏之精銳，盡萃於此。

translations.literal: But Wei's elite troops are all gathered here.
translations.idiomatic: But Wei's best troops are all gathered here.

sentences.zh: 犒師之禮，非無故事。

translations.literal: The custom of feasting the army is not without precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Feasting the army is not without precedent.

sentences.zh: 若殿下為設享會，因請於謹等為歡。

translations.literal: If Your Highness holds a feast and invites Yu Jin and the others to join in revelry—
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness holds a banquet and invites Yu Jin and the others to join the celebration—

sentences.zh: 彼無我虞，當相率而至，預伏武士，因而斃之。

translations.literal: they will not be on guard against us; they will come in a body. Hide warriors beforehand and strike them down.
translations.idiomatic: they will not be on their guard and will come in a body. Hide warriors beforehand and kill them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 分命果毅，掩其營壘，斬馘逋醜，俾無遣噍。

translations.literal: Dispatch the bold and resolute to surprise their camps, behead the fugitive villains, leaving not one alive.
translations.idiomatic: Send the boldest men to surprise their camps, cut down the fugitive villains, and leave not one alive.

sentences.zh: 江陵百姓，撫而安之，文武官寮，隨即詮授。

translations.literal: Comfort and settle the people of Jiangling; immediately assign civil and military officials to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Comfort and settle the people of Jiangling, and immediately appoint civil and military officials to their posts.

sentences.zh: 旣荷更生之惠，孰不忻戴聖明。

translations.literal: Once they have received the grace of rebirth, who would not rejoice to uphold your sagely brilliance?
translations.idiomatic: Once they have received the grace of new life, who would not gladly uphold your enlightened rule?

sentences.zh: 魏人攝息，未敢送死。

translations.literal: The Wei men will hold their breath and not dare court death.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops will hold their breath and not dare risk their lives.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯之徒，折簡可致。

translations.literal: Men like Wang Sengbian can be summoned with a simple letter.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Wang Sengbian can be summoned with a brief letter.

sentences.zh: 然後朝服濟江，入踐皇極，纘堯復禹，萬世一時。

translations.literal: Then, in court dress cross the Yangtze, ascend the imperial throne, carry on Yao and restore Yu—a moment for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Then, in court dress, cross the Yangtze, ascend the throne, carry on the legacy of Yao and restore that of Yu—a once-in-ten-thousand-generations opportunity.

sentences.zh: 晷刻之間，大功可立。

translations.literal: Within the space of a few hours, great merit can be established.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few hours, great success can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 古人雲：「天與不取，反受其咎，時至不行，反受其殃。」

translations.literal: The ancients said: "Heaven gives and you do not take—you will bear the blame; the time arrives and you do not act—you will suffer calamity."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "When Heaven offers and you do not take, you invite blame; when the moment comes and you do not act, you invite disaster."

sentences.zh: 願殿下恢弘遠畧，勿懷匹夫之行。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Highness enlarge your far-reaching design and do not cling to the conduct of a common man."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to broaden your far-reaching design and not cling to the scruples of a common man."

sentences.zh: 詧不從，謂德毅曰：「卿之此策，非不善也。

translations.literal: Cha did not agree and said to Deyi: "Your stratagem is not a poor one.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha refused and said to Yin Deyi, "Your plan is not a bad one.

sentences.zh: 然魏人待我甚厚，未可背德。

translations.literal: Yet the Wei have treated me very generously; I cannot betray their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: But the Wei have treated me very generously, and I cannot betray that kindness.

sentences.zh: 若遽為卿計，則鄧

translations.literal: If I hastily followed your plan, then Deng
translations.idiomatic: If I rashly adopted your plan, then—as the Duke of Qi said—

translations.literal: (Qi)
translations.idiomatic: (Qi)

sentences.zh: 〔祁〕侯所謂人將不食吾餘也。」

translations.literal: [Qi] the Marquis's saying—"People will not eat my leftovers."
translations.idiomatic: people would not eat my leftovers.'"

sentences.zh: 旣而闔城長幼，被虜入關，又失襄陽之地。

translations.literal: Before long, old and young throughout the city were taken captive and marched into the pass; the territory of Xiangyang was also lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, young and old throughout the city were taken captive and marched through the pass, and Xiangyang was lost as well.

sentences.zh: 詧乃追悔曰：「恨不用尹德毅之言，以至於是。」

translations.literal: Cha then looked back in regret and said: "I regret not having taken Yin Deyi's advice, which led to this."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha then looked back in regret and said, "I regret not having taken Yin Deyi's advice. It has brought me to this."

sentences.zh: 又見邑居殘毀，干戈日用，恥其威畧不振，常懷憂憤。

translations.literal: He also saw towns and dwellings in ruins, arms used daily; ashamed that his martial prestige did not revive, he constantly nursed grief and anger.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw towns and dwellings in ruins and arms in daily use. Ashamed that his power and prestige had not revived, he constantly nursed grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 乃著《愍時賦》以見意。

translations.literal: He then composed "Fu on Lamenting the Times" to express his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote "Fu on Lamenting the Times" to express his mind.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words read:
translations.idiomatic: Its words read:

sentences.zh: 嗟余命之舛薄，實賦運之逢屯。

translations.literal: Alas, my fate is perverse and thin; truly my allotted fortune meets with hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—my fate is crooked and thin; truly my allotted lot has met with hardship.

sentences.zh: 旣殷憂而彌歲，復坎壈以相鄰。

translations.literal: Already deep in sorrow for a full year, again adversity presses close beside me.
translations.idiomatic: Already sunk in sorrow for a full year, again hardship presses close at my side.

sentences.zh: 晝營營而至晚，夜耿耿而通晨。

translations.literal: By day I fret until evening; by night I lie awake straight through to dawn.
translations.idiomatic: By day I fret until evening falls; by night I lie awake straight through to dawn.

sentences.zh: 望否極而雲泰，何杳杳而無津。

translations.literal: I hoped that extreme ill would turn to fair skies—why is it so dim and pathless?
translations.idiomatic: I hoped that utter ill would turn to fair skies—why is the way so dim and without a ford?

sentences.zh: 悲晉璽之遷趙，痛漢鼎之移新。

translations.literal: Grieving that the Jin seal passed to Zhao; pained that the Han cauldron shifted to Xin.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that the Jin imperial seal passed to Zhao; I ache that the Han dynastic cauldron shifted to Xin.

sentences.zh: 無田、範之明畧，愧夷、齊之得仁。

translations.literal: Without Tian Dan and Fan Li's brilliant strategies; ashamed compared to Bo Yi and Shu Qi's attaining benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: I lack Tian Dan and Fan Li's brilliant designs; I am ashamed before Bo Yi and Shu Qi's attainment of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 遂胡顏而苟免，謂小屈而或申。

translations.literal: Thus bearing a shameful face I barely escaped, thinking a small humiliation might yet be redeemed.
translations.idiomatic: So I bear a shameful face and barely survive, telling myself a small humiliation may yet be redeemed.

sentences.zh: 豈妖沴之無已，何國步之長淪。

translations.literal: Can these evil portents never cease? Why does the nation's fortune long sink so low?
translations.idiomatic: Can these evil portents never end? Why does the nation's fortune sink so long and so low?

sentences.zh: 恨少生而輕弱，本無志於爪牙。

translations.literal: I regret being frail from youth; I never aspired to be claw or fang.
translations.idiomatic: I regret that from youth I was slight and weak and never aspired to be a warrior.

sentences.zh: 謝兩章之雄勇，恧二東之英華。

translations.literal: I defer to the heroic valor of the two Zhangs; I feel ashamed before the splendid talents of the two men of the east.
translations.idiomatic: I defer to the heroic valor of the two Zhangs; I blush before the brilliant talents of the two men of the east.

sentences.zh: 豈三石於杜鄠，異五馬於琅邪。

translations.literal: How could three Zhangs in Du and E compare with five Simas in Langye?
translations.idiomatic: How could three Zhangs at Du and E compare with five Simas at Langye?

sentences.zh: 直受性而好善，類蓬生之在麻。

translations.literal: Simply by nature I incline to goodness, like dodder growing among hemp.
translations.idiomatic: By nature I simply incline to goodness, like dodder growing among hemp.

sentences.zh: 冀無咎而沾慶，將保靜而蠲邪。

translations.literal: I hoped to escape blame and receive blessing, to keep quiet and ward off evil.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped to escape blame and share in blessing, to keep still and ward off evil.

sentences.zh: 何昊穹之弗惠，值上帝之紆奢。

translations.literal: Why does the vast heaven show no favor? I met a Lord on High who indulges extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Why does vast Heaven show no kindness? I have met a Lord on High who indulges in excess.

sentences.zh: 神州鞠為茂草，赤縣遶於長蛇。

translations.literal: The divine land has become luxuriant weeds; the red realm is encircled by long serpents.
translations.idiomatic: The divine land has turned to rank weeds; the red realm is encircled by long serpents.

sentences.zh: 徒仰天而太息，空撫衿而咨嗟。

translations.literal: In vain I look to heaven and sigh deeply; empty, I clutch my robe and lament.
translations.idiomatic: In vain I look to heaven and sigh; empty-handed, I clutch my robe and lament.

sentences.zh: 惟古人之有懷，尚或感於知己。

translations.literal: Ancient men who cherished ideals were sometimes moved by those who understood them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient men who cherished ideals were sometimes moved by one who understood them.

sentences.zh: 況托萼於霄極，寵渥流於無已。

translations.literal: How much more so, having been sheltered as a bud on heaven's summit—the gracious favor flowing without end.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for one sheltered as a bud on heaven's summit, with gracious favor flowing without end.

sentences.zh: 或小善而必褒，時片言而見美。

translations.literal: A small good deed was sure to be praised; sometimes a single word would win admiration.
translations.idiomatic: A small good deed was always praised; sometimes a single word would win admiration.

sentences.zh: 昔待罪於禹川，歷三考而無紀。

translations.literal: Once I served in the shadow of guilt at Yuchuan; passed three evaluations yet won no commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Once I served under a charge of guilt at Yuchuan and passed three evaluations without commendation.

sentences.zh: 獲免戾於明時，遂超隆於宗子。

translations.literal: I was spared punishment in an enlightened age and was then raised above the rank of imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: I was spared punishment in an enlightened age and was then raised above the other imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 始解印於稽山，即驅傳於湘水。

translations.literal: First I surrendered my seal at Mount Ji, then traveled post-haste to the Xiang River.
translations.idiomatic: First I surrendered my seal at Mount Ji, then traveled post-haste to the Xiang River.

sentences.zh: 彼南陽之舊國，實天漢之嘉祉。

translations.literal: That ancient realm of Nanyang was truly a blessed fortune from Heaven's Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: That ancient realm of Nanyang was truly a blessed gift from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 旣川岳之形勝，復龍躍之基趾。

translations.literal: Both blessed by river and mountain terrain, and the foundation where the dragon once sprang up.
translations.idiomatic: Blessed in river and mountain terrain, and the very ground where the dragon once sprang up.

sentences.zh: 此首賞之謬及，謂維城之足恃。

translations.literal: At first I wrongly thought this foremost reward would suffice, believing the shield-wall of the realm could be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: At first I wrongly thought this foremost reward enough, believing the bulwark of the realm could be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 值諸侯之攜貳，遂留滯於樊川。

translations.literal: When the regional lords turned disloyal, I was left stranded at Fanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the regional lords turned disloyal, I was left stranded at Fanchuan.

sentences.zh: 等勾踐之絕望，同重耳之終焉。

translations.literal: I shared Goujian's despair and Duke Wen of Jin's final exile.
translations.idiomatic: I shared Goujian's despair and Duke Wen of Jin's exile to the end.

sentences.zh: 望南枝而灑泣，或東顧而潺湲。

translations.literal: Gazing toward southern branches and shedding tears; sometimes looking east and weeping rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward the southern branch and shedding tears, sometimes looking east with streaming eyes.

sentences.zh: 歸歟之情何極，首丘之思邈然。

translations.literal: How boundless the longing to return! How distant the thought of the hill where one's head should rest in death!
translations.idiomatic: How boundless the longing to return! How distant the thought of the hill where my head should rest in death!

sentences.zh: 忽值魏師入討，于彼南荊。

translations.literal: Suddenly Wei troops arrived on punitive expedition in that southern Jing region.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly Wei armies came on punitive expedition into that southern Jing region.

sentences.zh: 旣車徒之赩赫，遂一鼓而陵城。

translations.literal: Their chariots and footsoldiers blazing bright; with one drum-beat they stormed the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Their chariots and footsoldiers blazed bright; with one drum-roll they stormed the walls.

sentences.zh: 同寤生之舍許，等小白之全邢。

translations.literal: Like Duke Zhuang of Zheng abandoning Xu; like Duke Huan of Qi sparing Xing's survival.
translations.idiomatic: Like Duke Zhuang of Zheng yielding Xu, like Duke Huan of Qi preserving Xing.

sentences.zh: 伊社稷之不泯，實有感於恩靈。

translations.literal: That the altars of state were not extinguished—truly one must feel gratitude to gracious power.
translations.idiomatic: That the altars of state were not extinguished—truly one must feel gratitude for gracious power.

sentences.zh: 矧吾人之固陋，迥飄薄於流萍。

translations.literal: How much more for one as crude and shallow as I—drifting far, thin as duckweed on the stream.
translations.idiomatic: How much more for one as crude and shallow as I—drifting far, thin as duckweed on the water.

sentences.zh: 忽沉滯於茲土，復期月而無成。

translations.literal: Suddenly stranded on this soil; another month passes with nothing achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly stranded on this soil, another month passes with nothing achieved.

sentences.zh: 昔方千而畿甸，今七里而盤縈。

translations.literal: Once a thousand square li of royal domain; now but seven li winding round.
translations.idiomatic: Once a thousand square li of royal domain; now but seven li winding round.

sentences.zh: 寡田邑而可賦，闕丘井而求兵。

translations.literal: Too few fields and settlements to levy taxes; lacking the well-and-military units needed to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Too few fields and settlements to levy taxes; too few well-and-military units from which to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 無河內之資待，同滎陽之未平。

translations.literal: Without Henei's resources to draw on; like Xingyang still unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Without Henei's resources to draw on, like Xingyang still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 夜騷騷而擊柝，晝孑孑而揚旌。

translations.literal: At night the watch alarms clatter; by day lonely banners are raised.
translations.idiomatic: At night the watch-clappers sound in alarm; by day lonely banners are raised.

sentences.zh: 烽淩雲而迥照，馬伏櫪而悲鳴。

translations.literal: Beacon fires pierce the clouds with distant glare; horses at the manger neigh in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Beacon fires pierce the clouds with distant glare; horses at the manger neigh in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 旣有懷於斯日，亦焉得而云寧。

translations.literal: With such cares on this day, how can I say I am at peace?
translations.idiomatic: With such cares upon me now, how can I say that I am at peace?

sentences.zh: 彼雲夢之舊都，乃標奇於昔者。

translations.literal: That ancient capital of Yunmeng was famed as marvelous in former days.
translations.idiomatic: That ancient capital of Yunmeng was famed as marvelous in days gone by.

sentences.zh: 驗往記而瞻今，何名高而實寡。

translations.literal: Checking the records of old against what I see today—why is the renown so high yet the reality so sparse?
translations.idiomatic: Checking the records of old against what I see today—why is the fame so high and the reality so thin?

sentences.zh: 寂寥井邑，荒涼原野。

translations.literal: Desolate are the wells and hamlets; wasted the fields and plains.
translations.idiomatic: Desolate are the wells and hamlets; wasted are the fields and plains.

sentences.zh: 徒揄揚於宋玉，空稱嗟於司馬。

translations.literal: Merely extolling Song Yu in praise; in vain sighing for Sima.
translations.idiomatic: I can only praise Song Yu in vain and sigh for Sima Xiangru in vain.

sentences.zh: 南方卑而歎屈，長沙濕而悲賈。

translations.literal: The southern region being base, one sighs for Qu Yuan; Changsha being damp, one mourns Jia Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the lowly South one sighs for Qu Yuan; in damp Changsha one mourns Jia Yi.

sentences.zh: 余家國之一匡，庶興周而祀夏。

translations.literal: My house had one corner of the realm, hoping to raise Zhou and sacrifice to Xia.
translations.idiomatic: My house held one corner of the realm, hoping to revive Zhou and keep sacrifice to Xia.

sentences.zh: 忽縈憂而北屈，豈年華之天假。

translations.literal: Suddenly grief coils and one bows north; how could the years be Heaven-given?
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly grief coils and I am humbled in the north—would Heaven ever grant me my allotted years?

sentences.zh: 加以狗盜鼠竊，蜂蠆狐狸。

translations.literal: Added to this: dog-thieves and rat-pilferers, bees, scorpions, and foxes.
translations.idiomatic: On top of it all come dog-thieves and rat-pilferers, venomous bees and scorpions, sly foxes.

sentences.zh: 羣圉隸而為寇，聚臧獲而成師。

translations.literal: Herds of stable-slaves become bandits; gathered bond-servants form armies.
translations.idiomatic: Herds of stable-slaves turn to raiding; gathered bond-servants muster into armies.

sentences.zh: 窺覦津渚，跋扈江眉。

translations.literal: Coveting the fords and islets; overbearing on the river's brow.
translations.idiomatic: They covet the fords and islets, swaggering along the river's edge.

sentences.zh: 屢征肇於殷歲，頻戰起於軒時。

translations.literal: Repeated campaigns began in the early years; frequent battles arose from the dawn era.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign after campaign began in the earliest years; battle after battle arose from the dawn of the realm.

sentences.zh: 有扈興於《夏典》，《採芑》著於《周詩》。

translations.literal: Youhu rose in the Xia Canon; "Gathering Artemisia" is recorded in the Zhou Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Youhu's rising is recorded in the Xia Canon; "Gathering Artemisia" appears in the Zhou Odes.

sentences.zh: 方叔振於蠻貊，伯禽捷於淮夷。

translations.literal: Fang Shu stirred among Man and Mo; Bo Qin was victorious over the Huai Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shu roused the tribes of Man and Mo; Bo Qin triumphed over the Huai Yi.

sentences.zh: 在逋穢其能幾，會斬馘而搴旗。

translations.literal: How long can fugitive rebels endure? Soon heads are cut and banners seized.
translations.idiomatic: How long can fleeing rebels hold out? Soon heads are severed and banners torn down.

sentences.zh: 彼積惡之必稔，豈天靈之我欺。

translations.literal: Those who heap evil must ripen in it—would Heaven's spirit deceive me?
translations.idiomatic: Wickedness heaped up must ripen in the end—would Heaven's spirit truly deceive me?

sentences.zh: 交川路之雲擁，理惆悵而未怡。

translations.literal: Crossroads and rivers clouded over; reason itself is melancholy and not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Crossroads and rivers lie shrouded in cloud; my heart stays troubled and cannot find peace.

sentences.zh: 詧在位八載，年四十四，保定二年二月，薨。

translations.literal: Cha reigned eight years, aged forty-four; in the second month of the second year of Baoding, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha reigned eight years and was forty-four when he died in the second month of the second year of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 其羣臣等葬之於平陵，諡曰宣皇帝，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: His ministers and others buried him at Pingling; posthumous title Emperor Xuan, temple name Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers buried him at Pingling, with the posthumous title Emperor Xuan and temple name Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 詧少有大志，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Cha from youth had great ambition and did not fuss over minor proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiao Cha had lofty ambitions and did not fuss over minor proprieties.

sentences.zh: 雖多猜忌，而知人善任使，撫將士有恩，能得其死力。

translations.literal: Though much given to suspicion, he knew men and appointed them well; in nurturing generals and soldiers he was gracious and could win their utmost exertion unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Though much given to suspicion, he knew how to choose men and use them well; he treated generals and soldiers with kindness and could win their utmost devotion unto death.

sentences.zh: 性不飲酒，安於儉素，事其母以孝聞。

translations.literal: By nature he did not drink wine; content with frugality and plainness; in serving his mother he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He did not drink by nature, was content with frugal simplicity, and was famed for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 又不好聲色，尤惡見婦人，雖相去數步，遙聞其臭。

translations.literal: He also disliked music and women; he especially hated seeing women—even several paces away he could smell them from afar.
translations.idiomatic: He also disliked music and women, and especially hated the sight of women; even several paces away he claimed he could smell them.

sentences.zh: 經御婦人之衣，不復更著。

translations.literal: Once he had worn a woman's garment, he never put it on again.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had worn a woman's garment, he never wore it again.

sentences.zh: 又惡見人髪，白事者必方便以避之。

translations.literal: He also hated seeing people's hair; those reporting business always found pretexts to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: He also hated the sight of human hair; those reporting business always found ways to avoid showing it.

sentences.zh: 其在東揚州頗放誕，省覽

translations.literal: While in eastern Yang Province he was rather unrestrained, in reviewing
translations.idiomatic: While serving in eastern Yang Province he was rather unrestrained in reviewing

translations.literal: (bo)
translations.idiomatic: (bo)

sentences.zh: 〔簿〕領，好為戲論之言，以此獲譏於世。

translations.literal: [records and] ledgers, he liked making playful talk, and on this account was ridiculed by the world.
translations.idiomatic: records and ledgers, he liked indulging in playful talk, and for this was ridiculed by the world.

sentences.zh: 篤好文義，所著文集十五卷，內典《華嚴》、《般若》、《法華》、《金光明義疏》四十六卷，竝行於世。

translations.literal: Deeply fond of literary meaning; his collected writings fifteen fascicles; Buddhist scriptures Avatamsaka, Prajna, Lotus, Golden Light with commentary forty-six fascicles—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted to literature and Buddhist doctrine, he wrote fifteen fascicles of collected works and forty-six fascicles of commentaries on the Avatamsaka, Prajna, Lotus, and Golden Light Sutras, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 詧疆土旣狹，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Cha's territory being narrow, he was often discontent in dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha's domain was narrow, and he was often discontent.

sentences.zh: 每誦「老馬伏櫪，志在千里。

translations.literal: Whenever he recited "An old horse at the manger still aspires to a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he recited "An old horse at the manger still yearns for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 烈士暮年，壯心不已」，未嘗不盱衡扼腕，歎咤者久之。

translations.literal: A brave man in his twilight years—his stalwart heart never ceases," he never failed to glare and clench his wrist, sighing and exclaiming for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: A hero in old age—his fighting spirit never fades," he never failed to glare and clench his fist, sighing and exclaiming for a long while.

sentences.zh: 遂以憂憤發背而殂。

translations.literal: Thereupon from worry and anger a back ailment arose and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He finally died of a back ailment brought on by worry and indignation.

sentences.zh: 高祖又命其太子巋嗣位，年號天保。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu again ordered his heir Kui to succeed the throne; reign title Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu again had his heir Xiao Kui succeed the throne, with the reign title Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 五年，陳湘州刺史華皎、巴州刺史戴僧朔竝來附。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Chen's Xiangzhou Inspector Hua Jiao and Bazhou Inspector Dai Sengshuo both came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Hua Jiao, Inspector of Xiangzhou under Chen, and Dai Sengshuo, Inspector of Bazhou, both came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 皎送其子玄響為質於巋，乃請兵伐陳。

translations.literal: Jiao sent his son Xuanxiang as hostage to Kui, then requested troops to attack Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao sent his son Xuanxiang as a hostage to Xiao Kui and then asked for troops to attack Chen.

sentences.zh: 巋上言其狀。

translations.literal: Kui memorialized to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui reported the situation to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔衛公直督荊州總管權景宣、大將軍元定等赴之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Duke Wei Gong Zhi to supervise Jingzhou Governor-General Quan Jingxuan, Grand General Yuan Ding, and others to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered Duke Wei Zhi to supervise Jingzhou Governor-General Quan Jingxuan, Grand General Yuan Ding, and others in marching to their aid.

sentences.zh: 巋亦遣其柱國王操率水軍二萬，會皎於巴陵。

translations.literal: Kui also sent his Pillar of State Wang Cao leading twenty thousand naval troops to join Jiao at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui also sent his Pillar of State Wang Cao with twenty thousand naval troops to join Jiao at Baling.

sentences.zh: 旣而與陳將吳明徹等戰於沌口，直軍不利，元定遂沒。

translations.literal: Shortly after, they fought Chen generals Wu Mingche and others at Dunkou; Zhi's army fared badly and Yuan Ding was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they fought Chen generals led by Wu Mingche at Dunkou; Zhi's army was defeated and Yuan Ding was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 巋大將軍李廣等亦為陳人所虜，長沙、巴陵竝陷於陳。

translations.literal: Kui's Grand General Li Guang and others were also captured by Chen men; Changsha and Baling both fell to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui's Grand General Li Guang and others were also captured by Chen forces, and both Changsha and Baling fell to Chen.

sentences.zh: 衛公直乃歸罪於巋之柱國殷亮。

translations.literal: Duke Wei Gong Zhi then blamed Kui's Pillar of State Yin Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wei Zhi then blamed Xiao Kui's Pillar of State Yin Liang for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 巋雖以退敗不獨在亮，然不敢違命，遂誅之。

translations.literal: Though Kui knew the defeat was not solely Liang's fault, he dared not disobey the order and so executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xiao Kui knew the defeat was not Liang's fault alone, he dared not disobey and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹乘勝攻剋巋河東郡，獲其守將許孝敬。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche pressed the victory to attack and seize Kui's Hedong Commandery, capturing its defending general Xu Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche pressed his advantage, attacked and seized Xiao Kui's Hedong Commandery, and captured its defender Xu Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 明年，明徹進寇江陵，引江水灌城。

translations.literal: The next year Mingche advanced against Jiangling, diverting the Yangzi to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Mingche advanced against Jiangling and diverted the Yangzi to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 巋出頓紀南以避其銳。

translations.literal: Kui went out and halted at Jinan to avoid their sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui withdrew to Jinan to avoid their onslaught.

sentences.zh: 江陵副總管高琳與其尚書僕射王操拒守。

translations.literal: Jiangling Deputy Governor-General Gao Lin and his Executive of the Masters of Writing Wang Cao held the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling Deputy Governor-General Gao Lin and Executive Wang Cao held the city in defense.

sentences.zh: 巋馬軍主馬武、吉徹等擊明徹，敗之。

translations.literal: Kui's Cavalry Commander Ma Wu, Ji Che, and others struck Mingche and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui's cavalry commanders Ma Wu and Ji Che attacked Mingche and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 明徹退保公安。

translations.literal: Mingche withdrew to hold Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche withdrew and defended Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 巋乃還江陵。

translations.literal: Kui then returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui then returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 巋之八年，陳又遣其司空章昭達來寇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kui's reign, Chen again sent its Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda to invade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xiao Kui's reign, Chen again sent its Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda to invade.

sentences.zh: 江陵總管陸騰及巋之將士擊走之。

translations.literal: Jiangling Governor-General Lu Teng and Kui's generals and soldiers drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling Governor-General Lu Teng and Xiao Kui's troops drove him off.

sentences.zh: 昭達又寇章陵之青泥。

translations.literal: Zhaoda again invaded Qingni in Zhangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda again invaded Qingni in Zhangling.

sentences.zh: 巋令其大將軍許世武赴援，大為昭達所破。

translations.literal: Kui ordered his Grand General Xu Shiwu to go to relieve them; he was greatly defeated by Zhaoda.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui sent his Grand General Xu Shiwu to relieve them, but Xu was heavily defeated by Zhaoda.

sentences.zh: 初，華皎、戴僧朔從衛公直與陳人戰敗，率其麾下數百人歸於巋。

translations.literal: At first, Hua Jiao and Dai Sengshuo followed Duke Wei Gong Zhi in defeat against Chen and led several hundred of their followers back to Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hua Jiao and Dai Sengshuo had followed Duke Wei Zhi against Chen, been defeated, and led several hundred followers back to Xiao Kui.

sentences.zh: 巋以皎為司空，封江夏郡公。

translations.literal: Kui made Jiao Minister of Works and enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiangxia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui made Jiao Minister of Works and enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 以僧朔為車騎將軍，封吳興縣侯。

translations.literal: He made Sengshuo General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He made Sengshuo General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 巋之十年，皎來朝。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kui's reign, Jiao came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xiao Kui's reign, Jiao came to court.

sentences.zh: 至襄陽，請衛公直曰：「梁主旣失江南諸郡，民少國貧。

translations.literal: Arriving at Xiangyang, he petitioned Duke Wei Gong Zhi, saying: "The Liang ruler has already lost the Jiangnan commanderies; the people are few and the state is poor.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he said to Duke Wei Zhi: "The Lord of Liang has already lost the Jiangnan commanderies; his people are few and his state is poor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷興亡繼絕，理宜資贍，豈使齊桓、楚莊獨擅救衛復陳之美。

translations.literal: The court in raising the fallen and continuing the extinguished ought properly to provide support—how can Duke Huan of Qi and King Zhuang of Chu alone monopolize the glory of rescuing Wei and restoring Chen?
translations.idiomatic: The court, in preserving states on the verge of extinction, ought properly to support them—must Duke Huan of Qi and King Zhuang of Chu alone monopolize the glory of saving Wei and restoring Chen?

sentences.zh: 望借數州，以裨梁國。」

translations.literal: I hope to borrow several prefectures to supplement the Liang state."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be lent several prefectures to strengthen the Liang state."

sentences.zh: 直然之，乃遣使言狀高祖。

translations.literal: Zhi approved, then sent an envoy to report the situation to Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi agreed and sent an envoy to report the matter to Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖許之，詔以基、平、鄀三州歸之於巋。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu granted it, decreeing that the three prefectures Ji, Ping, and E be returned to Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu granted the request and decreed that the three prefectures of Ji, Ping, and E be returned to Xiao Kui.

sentences.zh: 及高祖平齊，巋朝於鄴。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu pacified Qi, Kui had audience at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu conquered Qi, Xiao Kui had audience at Ye.

sentences.zh: 高祖雖以禮接之，然未之重也。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Gaozu received him with courtesy, he did not yet greatly esteem him.
translations.idiomatic: Although Emperor Gaozu received him courteously, he did not yet greatly esteem him.

sentences.zh: 巋知之，後因宴承間，乃陳其父荷太祖拯救之恩，幷敘二國艱虞，唇齒掎角之事。

translations.literal: Kui knew this; later at a banquet he seized an opening to set forth how his father owed Grand Ancestor the grace of rescue, and together narrated the two states' hard trials and their close, mutually supporting relation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui knew this; later, at a banquet, he seized an opportunity to speak of how his father owed the Grand Ancestor the grace of rescue, and of the two states' shared hardship and close, mutually supporting bond.

sentences.zh: 詞理辯暢，因涕泗交流。

translations.literal: His words and reasoning were fluent and eloquent; then tears and mucus streamed together.
translations.idiomatic: His words flowed with eloquence, and tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦為之歔欷。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu also sighed deeply for him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu also sighed deeply in response.

sentences.zh: 自是大加賞異，禮遇日隆。

translations.literal: From then on he greatly prized and distinguished him; courteous treatment daily grew loftier.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he greatly valued him, and Xiao Kui's honors grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 後高祖復與之宴，齊氏故臣吒列長义亦預焉。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Gaozu again banqueted with him; former Qi minister Tuoilie Chang Yi also attended.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Gaozu banqueted with him again, and Tuoilie Chang Yi, a former minister of Qi, was also present.

sentences.zh: 高祖指謂巋曰：「是登陴罵朕者也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu pointed and said to Kui: "That is the one who mounted the wall and cursed me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu pointed and said to Xiao Kui: "That is the man who mounted the wall and cursed me."

sentences.zh: 巋曰：「長义未能輔桀，飛敢吠堯。」

translations.literal: Kui said: "Chang Yi could not assist Jie—how dare Fei bark at Yao?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui said: "Chang Yi could not assist Jie—how dare a mere dog bark at Yao?"

sentences.zh: 高祖大笑。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 及酒酣，高祖又命琵琶自彈之。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, Emperor Gaozu again ordered the pipa and played it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had warmed, Emperor Gaozu had a pipa brought and played it himself.

sentences.zh: 仍謂巋曰：「當為梁主盡歡。」

translations.literal: He also said to Kui: "Let us give the Lord of Liang full merriment."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Xiao Kui: "We must give the Lord of Liang full merriment."

sentences.zh: 巋乃起，請舞。

translations.literal: Kui then rose and asked to dance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui then rose and asked to dance.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「梁主乃能為朕舞乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "Can the Lord of Liang actually dance for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: "Can the Lord of Liang really dance for me?"

sentences.zh: 巋曰：「陛下旣親撫五弦，臣何敢不同百獸。」

translations.literal: Kui said: "Your Majesty having personally played the five strings, how dare I fail to join the hundred beasts?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui said: "Since Your Majesty has personally strummed the five strings, how dare I fail to join the hundred beasts in dance?"

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，賜雜繒萬段、良馬數十匹，幷賜齊後主妓妾，及常所乘五百里駿馬以遺之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and granted ten thousand bolts of mixed silk, several dozen fine horses, and also gave him the concubines of the former Qi ruler and the five-hundred-li swift horse he usually rode as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and gave him ten thousand bolts of mixed silk, several dozen fine horses, the concubines of the former ruler of Qi, and the five-hundred-li stallion he usually rode.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝執政，尉遲迥、王謙、司馬消難等各起兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power, Yuwen Jiong, Wang Qian, Sima Xiaonan, and others each raised armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui came to power, Yuwen Jiong, Wang Qian, Sima Xiaonan, and others each raised armies in revolt.

sentences.zh: 時巋將帥皆密請興師，與迥等為連衡之勢，進可以盡節於周氏，退可以席捲山南。

translations.literal: At that time Kui's generals all secretly petitioned to raise troops and with Jiong and the others form a linked alliance; advancing they could show utmost loyalty to the Zhou house, retreating they could sweep up south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Kui's generals all secretly urged him to raise troops and join Jiong and the others in alliance—advancing, they could prove their loyalty to the Zhou house; retreating, they could sweep up the lands south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 巋固以為不可。

translations.literal: Kui firmly held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而消難奔陳，迥等相次破滅。

translations.literal: Before long Xiaonan fled to Chen; Jiong and the others were successively destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiaonan fled to Chen, and Jiong and the others were successively destroyed.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝旣踐極，恩禮彌厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui had ascended the throne, gracious treatment grew ever thicker.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Wen of Sui had ascended the throne, his gracious treatment grew ever more generous.

sentences.zh: 遣使賜金三百兩、銀一千兩、布帛萬段、馬五百匹。

translations.literal: He sent envoys granting three hundred liang of gold, one thousand liang of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with gifts of three hundred taels of gold, one thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，隋文帝備禮納巋女為晉王妃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, Emperor Wen of Sui with full rites took Kui's daughter as Princess of Jin's consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang, Emperor Wen of Sui formally took Xiao Kui's daughter as consort to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 又欲以其子瑒尚蘭陵公主。

translations.literal: He also wished to have his son Yang marry Princess Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to marry his son Yang to Princess Lanling.

sentences.zh: 由是罷江陵總管，巋專制其國。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Jiangling Governor-General post was abolished; Kui held sole authority over his state.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the post of Jiangling Governor-General was abolished, and Xiao Kui held sole authority over his state.

sentences.zh: 四年，巋來朝長安，隋文帝甚敬待之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Kui came to audience at Chang'an; Emperor Wen of Sui treated him with great respect.
