translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Xiao Kui came to court at Chang'an, and Emperor Wen of Sui received him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 詔巋位在王公之上，賜縑萬匹，珍玩稱是。

translations.literal: He decreed Kui's rank above kings and dukes, granting ten thousand bolts of fine silk and curios to match.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that Xiao Kui's rank should stand above kings and dukes, and gave him ten thousand bolts of fine silk and a matching store of rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 及還，親執其手謂之曰：「梁主久滯荊、楚，未復舊都，故鄉之念，良軫懷抱。

translations.literal: When he was returning, he personally took his hand and said: "The Lord of Liang has long lingered in Jing and Chu, not yet returned to the old capital; thoughts of home truly pierce the breast.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiao Kui was leaving, the emperor personally took his hand and said: "The Lord of Liang has long lingered in Jing and Chu and has not yet returned to his old capital; thoughts of home must weigh heavily on your heart.

sentences.zh: 朕當振旅長江，相送旋反耳。」

translations.literal: I shall marshal troops on the Yangzi and escort you home again."
translations.idiomatic: I shall marshal troops on the Yangzi and escort you home."

sentences.zh: 巋在位二十三載，年四十四，五年五月薨。

translations.literal: Kui reigned twenty-three years, aged forty-four; in the fifth month of the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui reigned twenty-three years and was forty-four when he died in the fifth month of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 其羣臣葬之於顯陵，諡曰孝

translations.literal: His ministers buried him at Xianling; posthumous title Xiao
translations.idiomatic: His ministers buried him at Xianling with the posthumous title Xiao

translations.literal: (wen)
translations.idiomatic: (wen)

sentences.zh: 〔明〕皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: [ming] Emperor, temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: [ming] Emperor, with temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 巋孝悌慈仁，有君人之量。

translations.literal: Kui was filial, fraternal, benevolent, and humane, with the measure of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui was filial, fraternal, benevolent, and humane, and had the makings of a true ruler.

sentences.zh: 四時祭享，未嘗不悲慕流涕。

translations.literal: At the four seasonal sacrifices he never failed to mourn with longing and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: At the four seasonal sacrifices he never failed to mourn with longing and weep.

sentences.zh: 性尤儉約，御下有方，境內稱治。

translations.literal: His nature was especially frugal and restrained; in governing subordinates he had method; within the borders he was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially frugal by nature, governed his subjects with skill, and his domain was considered well ordered.

sentences.zh: 所著《文集》及《孝經》、《周易義記》及《大小乘幽微》，竝行於世。

translations.literal: His Collected Works, Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Zhou Changes, and Profundities of Greater and Lesser Vehicles—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Works, commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Book of Changes, and Profundities of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝又命其太子蕭琮嗣位，年號廣運。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui again ordered his heir Xiao Cong to succeed the throne; reign title Guangyun.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui again had his heir Xiao Cong succeed the throne, with the reign title Guangyun.

sentences.zh: 琮字溫文。

translations.literal: Cong's courtesy name was Wenwen.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's courtesy name was Wenwen.

sentences.zh: 性倜儻不羈，博學有文義，兼善弓馬。

translations.literal: By nature unrestrained and free-spirited; broad in learning with literary accomplishment; also skilled in archery and horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: He was free-spirited and unconstrained by nature, broadly learned and accomplished in letters, and also skilled in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 初封東陽王，尋立為皇太子。

translations.literal: At first enfeoffed as King of Dongyang; soon established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as King of Dongyang and soon made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，隋文帝徵琮叔父岑入朝，因留不遣。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Emperor Wen of Sui summoned Cong's uncle Cen to court and thereupon detained him without sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong succeeded to the throne, Emperor Wen of Sui summoned his uncle Cen to court and kept him there, refusing to let him return.

sentences.zh: 復置江陵總管以監之。

translations.literal: The post of Regional Commander of Jiangling was again established to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: A Regional Commander was again installed at Jiangling to keep watch over the state.

sentences.zh: 琮之二年，隋文帝又徵琮入朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cong, Emperor Wen of Sui again summoned Cong to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cong's reign, Emperor Wen of Sui again summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 琮率其臣下二百餘人朝於長安。

translations.literal: Cong led more than two hundred of his ministers and subordinates to pay court at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Cong led more than two hundred of his ministers and officials to Chang'an to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝仍遣武鄉公崔弘度將兵戍江陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui still dispatched Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu to lead troops and garrison Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui still sent the Duke of Wuxiang, Cui Hongdu, to garrison Jiangling with troops.

sentences.zh: 軍至鄀州，琮叔父巖及弟

translations.literal: When the army reached E Prefecture, Cong's uncle Yan and his younger brother
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached E Prefecture, Cong's uncle Yan and his younger brother

translations.literal: (yan)
translations.idiomatic: (yan)

sentences.zh: 〔瓛〕等懼弘度掩襲之，遂虜居民奔於陳。

translations.literal: [Huan] and the others, fearing Hongdu would launch a surprise attack, then seized the people and fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan and the others, fearing that Hongdu would launch a surprise attack, abducted the populace and fled to Chen.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝於是廢梁國，曲赦江陵死罪，給民復十年。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui thereupon abolished the state of Liang, issued a limited amnesty for capital crimes in Jiangling, and granted the people a ten-year tax remission.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui thereupon abolished the Liang state, granted a limited amnesty for capital offenses in Jiangling, and gave the people a ten-year tax remission.

sentences.zh: 梁二主各給守墓十戶。

translations.literal: The two rulers of Liang were each given ten households to guard their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the two Liang rulers was granted ten households to tend their tombs.

sentences.zh: 尋拜琮為柱國，封莒國公。

translations.literal: Soon Cong was appointed Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was soon made Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 自詧初即位，歲在乙亥，至是，歲在丁未，凡三十有三歲矣。

translations.literal: From Cha's first accession, when the year was in yihai, until this time, when the year was in dingwei—the total was thirty-three years.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiao Cha's first accession in the year yihai until this time in dingwei, thirty-three years had passed in all.

sentences.zh: 詧子嶚，追諡孝惠太子；

translations.literal: Cha's son Yao, posthumously titled Filial and Gracious Crown Prince;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha's son Yao was posthumously titled Filial and Gracious Crown Prince;

sentences.zh: 巖，封安平王；

translations.literal: Yan, enfeoffed as Prince of Anping;
translations.idiomatic: Yan was enfeoffed as Prince of Anping;

sentences.zh: 岌，東平王；

translations.literal: Ji, Prince of Dongping;
translations.idiomatic: Ji was Prince of Dongping;

sentences.zh: 岑，河間王，後改封吳郡王。

translations.literal: Cen, Prince of Hejian, later changed to Prince of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cen was Prince of Hejian and later reassigned as Prince of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 巋子瓛，義興王；

translations.literal: Kui's son Huan, Prince of Yixing;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui's son Huan was Prince of Yixing;

sentences.zh: 瑑，晉陵王；

translations.literal: Zhuan, Prince of Jinling;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuan was Prince of Jinling;

sentences.zh: 璟，臨海王；

translations.literal: Jing, Prince of Linhai;
translations.idiomatic: Jing was Prince of Linhai;

sentences.zh: 珣，南海王；

translations.literal: Xun, Prince of Nanhai;
translations.idiomatic: Xun was Prince of Nanhai;

sentences.zh: 瑒，義安王；

translations.literal: Chang, Prince of Yi'an;
translations.idiomatic: Chang was Prince of Yi'an;

sentences.zh: 瑀，新安王。

translations.literal: Yu, Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 詧之在藩及居帝位，以蔡大寶為股肱，王操為腹心，魏益德、尹正、薛暉、許孝敬、薛宣為爪牙，甄玄成、劉盈、岑善方、傅准、褚珪、蔡大業典衆務。

translations.literal: While Cha was in his princely domain and when he occupied the imperial throne, he made Cai Dabao his right arm and Wang Cao his inner heart; Wei Yide, Yin Zheng, Xue Hui, Xu Xiaojing, and Xue Xuan were his claws and teeth; Zhen Xuancheng, Liu Ying, Cen Shanfang, Fu Zhun, Chu Gui, and Cai Daye handled the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiao Cha held his princely domain and after he took the throne, he relied on Cai Dabao as his right arm and Wang Cao as his trusted inner counselor; Wei Yide, Yin Zheng, Xue Hui, Xu Xiaojing, and Xue Xuan served as his strong hands; and Zhen Xuancheng, Liu Ying, Cen Shanfang, Fu Zhun, Chu Gui, and Cai Daye managed the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 張綰以舊齒處顯位，沉重以儒學蒙厚禮。

translations.literal: Zhang Wan, because of senior standing, held a conspicuous position; Chen Zhong, because of Confucian learning, received generous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wan held a prominent post by virtue of his seniority, while Chen Zhong was treated with great respect for his Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 自餘多所獎拔，咸盡其器能。

translations.literal: The rest he promoted in many places, all fully employing their talents.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest, he promoted many men and put each to full use according to his abilities.

sentences.zh: 及巋纂業，親賢竝用，將相則華皎、殷亮、劉忠義，宗室則蕭欣、蕭翼，民望則蕭確、謝溫、柳洋、王湜、徐岳，外戚則王凝、王誦、殷璉，文章則劉孝勝、范迪、沈君遊、君公、柳信言，政事則袁敞、柳莊、蔡延壽、甄詡、皇甫茲。

translations.literal: When Kui succeeded to the enterprise, he employed both kin and worthies together: as generals and ministers, Hua Jiao, Yin Liang, and Liu Zhongyi; among the imperial clan, Xiao Xin and Xiao Yi; men of public esteem, Xiao Que, Xie Wen, Liu Yang, Wang Shi, and Xu Yue; maternal relatives, Wang Ning, Wang Song, and Yin Lian; literary men, Liu Xiaosheng, Fan Di, Shen Junyou, Jungong, and Liu Xinyan; and for state affairs, Yuan Chang, Liu Zhuang, Cai Yanshou, Zhen Xu, and Huangfu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Kui succeeded to the throne, he employed both kinsmen and worthy men: among generals and ministers were Hua Jiao, Yin Liang, and Liu Zhongyi; among the imperial clan, Xiao Xin and Xiao Yi; men held in public esteem, Xiao Que, Xie Wen, Liu Yang, Wang Shi, and Xu Yue; maternal relatives, Wang Ning, Wang Song, and Yin Lian; literary men, Liu Xiaosheng, Fan Di, Shen Junyou, Jungong, and Liu Xinyan; and for governance, Yuan Chang, Liu Zhuang, Cai Yanshou, Zhen Xu, and Huangfu Ci.

sentences.zh: 故能保其疆土，而和其民人焉。

translations.literal: Thus they were able to preserve their territory and harmonize their people.
translations.idiomatic: In this way they were able to preserve their territory and keep their people at peace.

sentences.zh: 今載詧子嶚等及蔡大寶以下尤著者，附於左。

translations.literal: Now the biographies of Cha's son Yao and others, and of the most notable men from Cai Dabao downward, are appended below.
translations.idiomatic: What follows are accounts of Xiao Cha's son Yao and others, together with the most notable men from Cai Dabao downward.

sentences.zh: 其在梁、陳、隋已有傳，及巋諸子未任職者，則不兼錄。

translations.literal: Those who already have biographies in the histories of Liang, Chen, and Sui, and Kui's sons who had not yet taken office, are not included here as well.
translations.idiomatic: Those who already have biographies in the histories of Liang, Chen, and Sui, and Xiao Kui's sons who had not yet held office, are not included here.

sentences.zh: 嶚字道遠，詧之長子也。

translations.literal: Yao's courtesy name was Daoyuan; he was Cha's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, whose courtesy name was Daoyuan, was Xiao Cha's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰宣靜皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Xuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，有成人之量。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and keen, with the measure of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and precocious, showing the maturity of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 詧之為梁主，立為世子。

translations.literal: When Cha became ruler of Liang, Yao was established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha became ruler of Liang, he was made heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 及詧稱帝，追諡焉。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor, he was posthumously titled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor, he was posthumously ennobled.

sentences.zh: 巖字義遠，詧第五子也。

translations.literal: Yan's courtesy name was Yiyuan; he was Cha's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, whose courtesy name was Yiyuan, was Xiao Cha's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 性仁厚，善於撫接。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and generous, skilled at comforting and receiving people.
translations.idiomatic: He was benevolent and generous by nature, and skilled at putting people at ease.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、荊州刺史、尚書令、太尉、太傅。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Palace Attendant, Regional Inspector of Jingzhou, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Commandant, and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Palace Attendant, Regional Inspector of Jingzhou, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Commandant, and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 入陳，授平東將軍、東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Entering Chen, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Regional Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Chen territory, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Regional Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，百姓推巖為主，以禦隋師。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, the common people raised Yan as their leader to resist the Sui army.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, the people set Yan up as their leader to resist the Sui armies.

sentences.zh: 為總管宇文述所破，伏法於長安。

translations.literal: He was defeated by Regional Commander Yuwen Shu and was executed by law at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated by the Regional Commander Yuwen Shu and executed at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 岌，詧第六子也。

translations.literal: Ji was Cha's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was Xiao Cha's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 性淳和，幼而好學。

translations.literal: By nature he was simple and harmonious; from youth he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and even-tempered by nature, and loved learning from childhood.

sentences.zh: 位至侍中、中衛將軍。

translations.literal: He rose to the posts of Palace Attendant and General of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the posts of Palace Attendant and General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 巋之五年，卒，贈侍中、司空。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kui, he died; posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiao Kui's reign he died and was posthumously granted the posts of Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 諡曰孝。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Filial.

sentences.zh: 岑字智遠，詧第八子也。

translations.literal: Cen's courtesy name was Zhiyuan; he was Cha's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Cen, whose courtesy name was Zhiyuan, was Xiao Cha's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 位至太尉。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 性簡貴，御下嚴整。

translations.literal: By nature he was reserved and noble; in governing subordinates he was strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was reserved and proud by nature, and strict and orderly in governing his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 及琮嗣位，自以望重屬尊，頗有不法，故隋文徵入朝。

translations.literal: When Cong succeeded to the throne, Cen considered himself weighty in prestige and close in kinship, and behaved with considerable impropriety; therefore Emperor Wen of Sui summoned him to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong succeeded to the throne, Cen considered himself eminent in prestige and close in kinship, and behaved with considerable impropriety; for this reason Emperor Wen of Sui summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 拜大將軍，封懷義郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyi.

sentences.zh: 瓛字欽文，巋第三子也。

translations.literal: Huan's courtesy name was Qinwen; he was Kui's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, whose courtesy name was Qinwen, was Xiao Kui's third son.

sentences.zh: 幼有令譽，能屬文，特為巋所愛。

translations.literal: From youth he had an excellent reputation, was able to compose literary works, and was especially beloved by Kui.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he enjoyed an excellent reputation, could compose literary works, and was especially beloved by Xiao Kui.

sentences.zh: 位至荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，隋師至鄀州，梁之百寮咸恐懼，計無所出。

translations.literal: At first, when the Sui army reached E Prefecture, all the officials of Liang were alike in fear and could think of no plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui army first reached E Prefecture, all the officials of Liang were terrified and could think of no plan.

sentences.zh: 唯瓛建議南奔。

translations.literal: Only Huan proposed fleeing south.
translations.idiomatic: Only Huan proposed fleeing south.

sentences.zh: 入陳，授侍中、安東將軍、吳州刺史。

translations.literal: Entering Chen, he was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Regional Inspector of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Chen, he was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Regional Inspector of Wu.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，吳人推為主以御隋師。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, the people of Wu raised him as their leader to resist the Sui army.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, the people of Wu set him up as their leader to resist the Sui armies.

sentences.zh: 戰而敗，與巖同時伏法。

translations.literal: He fought and was defeated, and was executed by law at the same time as Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated in battle and executed at the same time as Yan.

sentences.zh: 蔡大寶字敬位，濟陽考城人。

translations.literal: Cai Dabao's courtesy name was Jingwei; he was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Dabao, whose courtesy name was Jingwei, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖履，齊尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lu was Director of the Department of Sacrificial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lu served as Director of the Department of Sacrificial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父點，梁尚書儀曹郎、南兗州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Dian was Director of the Department of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites of Liang and Vice Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dian served as Director of the Department of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites of Liang and as Vice Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 大寶少孤，而篤學不倦，善屬文。

translations.literal: Dabao lost his father while young, yet studied with tireless devotion and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Dabao was orphaned in youth, yet studied with tireless devotion and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 初以明經對策第一，解褐武陵王國左常侍。

translations.literal: At first, ranking first in the Classics examination by written response, he left commoner status to become Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He first ranked first in the Classics examination and left commoner status to become Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 嘗以書干僕射徐勉，大為勉所賞異。

translations.literal: Once he presented a letter to Vice Director Xu Mian and was greatly admired and singled out for distinction by Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent a letter to Vice Director Xu Mian and was greatly admired by him.

sentences.zh: 乃令與其子遊處，所有墳籍，盡以給之。

translations.literal: Mian then had him associate and spend time with his son, and gave him all the books in his collection.
translations.idiomatic: Mian then had him keep company with his son and gave him all the books in his library.

sentences.zh: 遂博覽羣書，學無不綜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he read widely among all books, and in learning there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he read widely and mastered every branch of learning.

sentences.zh: 詧初出第，勉仍薦大寶為侍讀，兼掌記室。

translations.literal: When Cha first left his princely residence, Mian still recommended Dabao as Reader-in-Waiting and concurrently put him in charge of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha first left his princely residence, Mian recommended Dabao as Reader-in-Waiting and put him in charge of the secretariat as well.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Department of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Director of the Department of Ceremonial Affairs in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出鎮會稽，大寶為記室，領長流。

translations.literal: When Cha went out to govern Kuaiji, Dabao served as secretarial officer and concurrently headed the senior staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha went out to govern Kuaiji, Dabao served as secretarial officer and headed the senior staff.

sentences.zh: 詧蒞襄陽，遷諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Cha arrived at Xiangyang, Dabao was transferred to the post of Advisory Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha arrived at Xiangyang, Dabao was transferred to the post of Advisory Aide.

sentences.zh: 及梁元帝與河東王譽結隙，詧令大寶使江陵以觀之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang and Prince of Hedong Yu became estranged, Cha sent Dabao on a mission to Jiangling to observe the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang and the Prince of Hedong, Xiao Yu, became estranged, Xiao Cha sent Dabao to Jiangling to observe the situation.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝素知大寶，見之甚悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang had long known Dabao, and on seeing him was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang had long known Dabao, and was greatly pleased to see him.

sentences.zh: 乃示所制《玄覽賦》，令注解焉。

translations.literal: He then showed the "Xuanlan Fu" he had composed and ordered Dabao to annotate it.
translations.idiomatic: He then showed him the "Xuanlan Fu" he had composed and ordered him to write a commentary on it.

sentences.zh: 三日而畢。

translations.literal: In three days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He finished it in three days.

sentences.zh: 元帝大嗟賞之，贈遺甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan greatly admired and praised it, and gave him very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan greatly admired it and gave him very generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 大寶還白詧云：「湘東必有異圖，禍亂將作，不可下援臺城。」

translations.literal: Dabao returned and reported to Cha: "The Prince of Xiangdong must harbor ulterior designs; calamity and disorder are about to break out; one must not descend to aid Taicheng."
translations.idiomatic: Dabao returned and reported to Xiao Cha, "The Prince of Xiangdong must harbor ulterior designs; calamity and disorder are about to break out. We must not go down to aid Taicheng."

sentences.zh: 詧納之。

translations.literal: Cha accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 及為梁主，除中書侍郎，兼吏部，掌大選事，領襄陽太守，遷員外散騎常侍、吏部郎，俄轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Cha became ruler of Liang, Dabao was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently in the Ministry of Personnel, in charge of major selection affairs, and concurrently Governor of Xiangyang; he was transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and soon became Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha became ruler of Liang, Dabao was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and major selection affairs, while also serving as Governor of Xiangyang; he was then promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and soon became Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 軍國之事，咸委決焉。

translations.literal: Military and state affairs were all entrusted to his decision.
translations.idiomatic: Military and state affairs were all entrusted to his judgment.

sentences.zh: 加授大將軍，遷尚書僕射，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Grand General, transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and advanced in title to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Grand General, promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and given the title General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 又除使持節、宣惠將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Proclaims Grace, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Proclaims Grace, and Regional Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 詧於江陵稱帝，徵為侍中、尚書令，參掌選事，又加雲麾將軍，荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor at Jiangling, Dabao was summoned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, participating in selection affairs; he was also given the additional title General of the Cloudy Pennant and Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor at Jiangling, Dabao was summoned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat to participate in selection affairs, and was also given the additional titles General of the Cloudy Pennant and Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 進位柱國、軍師將軍，領太子少傅，轉安前將軍，封安豐縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Pillar of State and General of the Army, concurrently Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, transferred to General Who Secures the Front, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfeng County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Pillar of State and General of the Army, made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, transferred to General Who Secures the Front, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Anfeng with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從巋入朝，領太子少傅。

translations.literal: Following Kui to court, he concurrently served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Xiao Kui to court, he served concurrently as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 巋嗣位，冊授司空、中書監、中權大將軍，領吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Kui succeeded to the throne, Dabao was invested by decree as Minister of Works, Supervisor of the Secretariat, Grand General of Central Authority, and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Kui succeeded to the throne, Dabao was invested by decree as Minister of Works, Supervisor of the Secretariat, Grand General of Central Authority, and concurrently Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 固讓司空，許之。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the post of Minister of Works, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the post of Minister of Works, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 加特進。

translations.literal: He was additionally granted the honorary title of Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally granted the honorary title of Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 巋之三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kui, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiao Kui's reign, he died.

sentences.zh: 巋哭之慟，自卒及葬，三臨其喪。

translations.literal: Kui wept for him in deep grief; from death until burial, he visited the mourning hall three times.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui wept for him in deep grief and visited his mourning hall three times from death until burial.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister over the Masses and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the post of Minister over the Masses and advanced in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文凱。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Literary and Triumphant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Literary and Triumphant.

sentences.zh: 配食詧廟。

translations.literal: He was granted a place in sacrifice at Cha's temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a place in sacrifice at Xiao Cha's temple.

sentences.zh: 大寶性嚴整，有智謀，雅達政事，文詞贍速。

translations.literal: Dabao was by nature strict and orderly, possessed wisdom and stratagem, was elegantly versed in state affairs, and was rich and swift in literary expression.
translations.idiomatic: Dabao was strict and orderly by nature, possessed wisdom and stratagem, was elegantly versed in state affairs, and wrote with richness and speed.

sentences.zh: 詧之章表書記教令詔冊，並大寶專掌之。

translations.literal: Cha's memorials, letters, records, instructions, edicts, and investiture documents were all exclusively handled by Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha's memorials, letters, records, instructions, edicts, and investiture documents were all handled exclusively by Dabao.

sentences.zh: 詧推心委任，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Cha entrusted him with open heart and made him his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha trusted him completely and made him his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 時人以詧之有大寶猶劉先主之有孔明焉。

translations.literal: People of the time said that Cha having Dabao was like Liu the Founding Lord having Kongming.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said that Xiao Cha having Dabao was like Liu Bei having Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 所著文集三十卷，及《尚書義疏》竝行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings in thirty volumes, together with his "Commentary on the Meaning of the Documents," both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings in thirty volumes, together with his Commentary on the Meaning of the Documents, both circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 有四子。

translations.literal: He had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons.

sentences.zh: 次子延壽，有器識，博涉經籍，尤善當世之務。

translations.literal: The second son, Yanshou, had capacity and discernment, ranged broadly through the classics and records, and was especially skilled in the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Yanshou, had capacity and discernment, ranged broadly through the classics and records, and was especially skilled in the affairs of his age.

sentences.zh: 尚詧女宣成公主。

translations.literal: He married Cha's daughter, Princess Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He married Xiao Cha's daughter, Princess Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 歷中書郎、尚書右丞、吏部郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Gentleman of the Secretariat, Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Gentleman of the Secretariat, Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Imperial Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 從琮入隋，授開府儀同三司，秘書丞。

translations.literal: Following Cong into Sui, he was granted the honors of General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank and appointed Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Xiao Cong into Sui territory, he was granted the honors of General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank and appointed Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 終於成州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his life as Regional Inspector of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Regional Inspector of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 大寶弟大業。

translations.literal: Dabao's younger brother was Daye.
translations.idiomatic: Dabao's younger brother was Daye.

sentences.zh: 大業字敬道。

translations.literal: Daye's courtesy name was Jingdao.
translations.idiomatic: Daye, whose courtesy name was Jingdao.

sentences.zh: 有至行，父沒，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: He possessed supreme conduct; when his father died, he observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of supreme filial devotion; when his father died, he observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 性寬恕，學涉經史，有將命材，屢充使詣闕。

translations.literal: By nature he was forgiving and generous; his learning ranged through the classics and histories; he had the talent for emissary missions and repeatedly served as envoy to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: He was forgiving and generous by nature, widely read in the classics and histories, and possessed the talent of an envoy; he repeatedly served as ambassador to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 初以西中郎府參軍隨詧之鎮。

translations.literal: At first he served as Military Adjutant of the Western Central Commandery headquarters and followed Cha to his commandery post.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Military Adjutant of the Western Central Commandery headquarters and followed Xiao Cha to his territorial post.

sentences.zh: 詧稱帝，歷尚書左丞、開遠將軍、監利郡守、散騎常侍、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor, he successively held the posts of Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, General Who Opens the Way, Administrator of Jianli Commandery, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Minister Steward.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor, Daye served successively as Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, General Who Opens the Way, Administrator of Jianli Commandery, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Minister Steward.

sentences.zh: 巋嗣位，遷都官尚書，除貞毅將軍、漳川太守。

translations.literal: When Kui succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Justice and appointed General of Unwavering Resolve and Administrator of Zhangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Kui succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Justice and appointed General of Unwavering Resolve and Administrator of Zhangchuan.

sentences.zh: 入為左民尚書、太常卿。

translations.literal: He entered court service as Director of the Ministry of the Left Household and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as Director of the Ministry of the Left Household and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 巋之七年，卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kui, he died; posthumously granted the status of Grand Master of Golden Bells and Ceremonial Grandees.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiao Kui's reign he died and was posthumously granted the status of Grand Master of Golden Bells and Ceremonial Grandees.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Simple.

sentences.zh: 有五子，允恭最知名。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Yun'gong was the most famous.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons; Yun'gong was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: He began his career as Assistant Editor in the Imperial Library and Domestic Companion to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Assistant Editor in the Imperial Library and Domestic Companion to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 梁滅入陳，拜尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: When Liang fell and he entered Chen, he was appointed Director of the Warehouse Bureau in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell and he entered Chen territory, he was appointed Director of the Warehouse Bureau in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，授起居舍人。

translations.literal: When Chen fell and he entered Sui, he was granted the post of Registrar of the Heir Apparent's Activities.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell and he entered Sui territory, he was appointed Registrar of the Heir Apparent's Activities.

sentences.zh: 王操字子高。

translations.literal: Wang Cao's courtesy name was Zigao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cao's courtesy name was Zigao.

sentences.zh: 其先，太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: His ancestors were from Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 詧母龔氏之外弟也。

translations.literal: He was the younger brother of Cha's mother, Lady Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was the younger brother of Xiao Cha's mother, Lady Gong.

sentences.zh: 祖靈慶，海鹽令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingqing served as Magistrate of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingqing served as Magistrate of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 父景休，臨川內史。

translations.literal: His father Jingxiu was Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingxiu was Administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 操性敦厚，有籌畧，博涉經史，在公恪勤。

translations.literal: Cao was by nature solid and generous, possessed of strategic insight, extensively learned in the classics and histories, and in office was scrupulous and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Cao was solid and generous by nature, possessed of strategic insight, widely read in the classics and histories, and scrupulously diligent in office.

sentences.zh: 初為詧外兵參軍，親任亞於蔡大寶。

translations.literal: At first he served as External Military Adjutant under Cha, and in personal trust was second only to Cai Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as External Military Adjutant under Xiao Cha, and in personal trust ranked second only to Cai Dabao.

sentences.zh: 詧承制，除尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Cao was made Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, he was made Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及稱帝，遷五兵尚書、大將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor, he was promoted to Director of the Five Armies Ministry, Grand General, and Regional Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor, he was promoted to Director of the Five Armies Ministry, Grand General, and Regional Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋進位柱國，封新康縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinkang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon advanced to Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinkang County.

sentences.zh: 巋嗣位，授鎮右將軍、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: When Kui succeeded to the throne, he was granted the post of General Who Guards the Right and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Kui succeeded to the throne, he was granted the post of General Who Guards the Right and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹為寇，巋出頓紀南，操撫循將士，莫不用命。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche raided as an invader, Kui went out and encamped at Jinan; Cao comforted and rallied the troops, and none failed to obey his orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche invaded, Xiao Kui marched out and encamped at Jinan; Cao comforted and rallied the troops, and all obeyed his commands without fail.

sentences.zh: 明徹旣退，江陵獲全，操之力也。

translations.literal: Once Mingche had withdrawn, Jiangling was preserved intact; this was due to Cao's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mingche had withdrawn, Jiangling was preserved intact—thanks to Cao's efforts.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、中衛將軍、尚書令、開府儀同三司，參掌選事，領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, General of the Central Guard, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank; he participated in managing selections for office and served concurrently as Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant, General of the Central Guard, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank; he participated in managing official appointments and concurrently served as Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 操旣位居朝右，每自挹損，深得當時之譽。

translations.literal: Once Cao held the highest position at court, he always restrained himself and humbled his rank, and thereby won deep renown among his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cao held the highest position at court, he always restrained himself and never exalted his rank, and thereby won deep renown among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 巋之十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kui, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Xiao Kui's reign he died.

sentences.zh: 巋舉哀於朝堂，流涕謂其羣臣曰：「天不使吾平蕩江表，何奪吾賢相之速也。」

translations.literal: Kui mourned him in the audience hall, weeping as he said to his assembled ministers: "Heaven does not allow me to pacify and sweep clean the lands south of the Yangtze—why has it taken my worthy minister so soon?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui mourned him in the audience hall and, weeping, said to his assembled ministers: "Heaven does not allow me to pacify the lands south of the Yangtze—why has it taken my worthy minister so soon?"

sentences.zh: 及葬，親祖於瓦官門。

translations.literal: At the burial, he personally led the funeral procession at Wagon-Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial, Xiao Kui personally led the funeral procession at the Wagon-Gate.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works; his title was advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works and his title was advanced to Duke.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康節。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Kangjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Kangjie.

sentences.zh: 有七子。

translations.literal: He had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 次子衡最知名。

translations.literal: His second son Heng was the most famous.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Heng was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 有才學，起家秘書郎。

translations.literal: Talented and learned, he began his career as Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and learned, he began his career as Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歷太子洗馬、中書、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Groom-in-Waiting to the Heir Apparent, Gentleman of the Secretariat, and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Groom-in-Waiting to the Heir Apparent, Gentleman of the Secretariat, and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 魏益德，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Yide was a native of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yide came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 有才幹，膽勇過人。

translations.literal: He had talent and administrative ability; his courage and daring surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: He had talent and administrative ability, and his courage and daring surpassed other men.

sentences.zh: 數從軍征討，以功累遷至郡守。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed armies on campaigns; through merit he was promoted by stages until he reached the rank of commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly followed armies on campaign and, through accumulated merit, was promoted by stages until he reached the rank of commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 詧蒞襄陽，以益德為其府司馬。

translations.literal: When Cha took up his post at Xiangyang, he appointed Yide military secretary of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha took up his post at Xiangyang, he appointed Yide military secretary of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 詧承制，拜將軍。

translations.literal: When Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Yide was given the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Yide was given the rank of general.

sentences.zh: 尋加大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 及詧稱帝，進位柱國，封上黃縣侯，邑千戶，加車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor, Yide was advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanghuang County with a fief of one thousand households, and additionally appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor, Yide was advanced to Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanghuang County with a fief of one thousand households, and additionally appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 詧之二年，卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cha, he died; posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiao Cha's reign he died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal and Stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Loyal and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: His title was advanced to Duke.

sentences.zh: 巋之五年，以益德配食詧廟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kui, Yide was given a place in sacrifice at Cha's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiao Kui's reign, Yide was given a place in sacrifice at Xiao Cha's temple.

sentences.zh: 尹正，其先天水人。

translations.literal: Yin Zheng — his ancestors were from Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zheng's ancestors came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 詧蒞雍州，正為其府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Cha took up his post at Yongzhou, Zheng served as Central Military Adjutant of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha took up his post at Yongzhou, Zheng served as Central Military Adjutant of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 擒張纘，獲杜岸，皆正之力。

translations.literal: The capture of Zhang Zuan and Du An were all due to Zheng's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: The captures of Zhang Zuan and Du An were both due to Zheng's efforts.

sentences.zh: 詧承制，以為將軍。

translations.literal: When Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Zheng was made a general.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Zheng was made a general.

sentences.zh: 尋拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 及稱帝，除護軍將軍，進位柱國，封新野縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Cha declared himself emperor, Zheng was appointed General Who Protects the Army, advanced to Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinye County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor, Zheng was appointed General Who Protects the Army, advanced to Pillar of State, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinye County with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 詧之三年，卒，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cha, he died; posthumously granted General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiao Cha's reign he died and was posthumously granted General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 諡曰剛。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Resolute.

sentences.zh: 巋之五年，以正配食詧廟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kui, Zheng was given a place in sacrifice at Cha's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xiao Kui's reign, Zheng was given a place in sacrifice at Xiao Cha's temple.

sentences.zh: 子德毅，多權畧，位至大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Deyi was versed in many stratagems and rose to the rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Deyi was versed in many stratagems and rose to the rank of Grand General.

sentences.zh: 後以見疑賜死。

translations.literal: Later, because he came under suspicion, he was granted death by imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he came under suspicion, he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 薛暉，河東人也。

translations.literal: Xue Hui was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Hui came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 有才畧。

translations.literal: He had talent and strategic insight.
translations.idiomatic: He had talent and strategic insight.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，形貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet in height and was imposing in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall and was imposing in appearance.

sentences.zh: 嘗督禁旅，為詧爪牙，當禦侮之任。

translations.literal: He once supervised the palace guard corps, serving as Cha's strong right hand and bearing the duty of repelling insult and aggression.
translations.idiomatic: He once supervised the palace guard corps, serving as Xiao Cha's strong right hand and bearing the duty of repelling invasion.

sentences.zh: 與尹正攻獲杜岸於南陽。

translations.literal: Together with Yin Zheng he attacked and captured Du An at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yin Zheng he attacked and captured Du An at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 詧承制，拜將軍。

translations.literal: When Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Hui was given the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Hui was given the rank of general.

sentences.zh: 尋加大將軍，進位柱國，除領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Grand General, advanced to Pillar of State, and appointed General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Grand General, advanced to Pillar of State, and appointed General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 巋之二年，卒，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kui, he died; posthumously granted General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiao Kui's reign he died and was posthumously granted General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 有六子，子建、子尚知名。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Zijian and Zishang were the best known.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; Zijian and Zishang were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 許孝敬，吳人，小名嗣兒。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaojing was a man of Wu; his childhood name was Si'er.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaojing was a man of Wu; his childhood name was Si'er.

sentences.zh: 勁勇過人，為詧驍將。

translations.literal: His vigor and bravery surpassed other men, and he was one of Cha's fiercest generals.
translations.idiomatic: His vigor and bravery surpassed other men, and he was one of Xiao Cha's fiercest generals.

sentences.zh: 以大將軍守河東。

translations.literal: He held Hedong as Grand General in garrison.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand General he held Hedong in garrison.

sentences.zh: 旣無救援，為吳明徹所擒，遂戮於建康市。

translations.literal: With no relief coming, he was captured by Wu Mingche and thereupon executed in the marketplace at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: With no relief coming, he was captured by Wu Mingche and executed in the marketplace at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子世武嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shi Wu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Wu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 少襲父大將軍，好勇不拘行檢。

translations.literal: From youth he inherited his father's rank as Grand General; he loved daring deeds and did not restrain his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he inherited his father's rank as Grand General; he loved daring deeds and paid little heed to propriety.

sentences.zh: 重賓客，施與不節。

translations.literal: He esteemed guests and gave away gifts without limit.
translations.idiomatic: He esteemed guests and gave away gifts without restraint.

sentences.zh: 資產旣盡，鬱鬱不得志，遂謀奔陳。

translations.literal: Once his assets were exhausted, he grew despondent and frustrated, and thereupon plotted to flee to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Once his assets were exhausted, he grew despondent and frustrated, and plotted to flee to Chen.

sentences.zh: 事覺，伏誅。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 又有大將軍李廣，會稽人。

translations.literal: There was also Grand General Li Guang, a man of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Grand General Li Guang, a native of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 早事詧，以敢勇聞。

translations.literal: He entered Cha's service early and was known for bold courage.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Xiao Cha's service early and was known for bold courage.

sentences.zh: 沌口之役，先登力戰。

translations.literal: At the battle of Dunningkou he was first to climb the walls and fought with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Dunningkou he was first to scale the heights and fought with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 及華皎軍敗，為吳明徹所擒。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao's army was defeated, Guang was captured by Wu Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao's army was defeated, Li Guang was captured by Wu Mingche.

sentences.zh: 將降之，廣辭色不屈，遂被害。

translations.literal: When they were about to accept his surrender, Guang refused to yield in speech or countenance, and was therefore killed.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to accept his surrender, Li Guang refused to yield in word or countenance, and was therefore killed.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，追封建興縣公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Commandant and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jianxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jianxing County.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 甄玄成字敬平，中山人。

translations.literal: Zhen Xuancheng's courtesy name was Jingping; he was a native of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Xuancheng, whose courtesy name was Jingping, came from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 博達經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: He was widely versed in the classics and histories and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely versed in the classics and histories and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 少為簡文所知。

translations.literal: From youth he was recognized by Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was recognized by Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 以錄事參軍隨詧鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: He served as Recording Secretary and followed Cha when Cha took up his post at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Recording Secretary and followed Xiao Cha when the latter took up his post at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 轉中記室參軍，掌書記，頗參政事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Chief of Records, kept the written records, and took part in government affairs to a considerable degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Central Chief of Records, kept the written records, and participated in government affairs to a considerable degree.

sentences.zh: 以江陵甲兵殷盛，遂懷貳心。

translations.literal: Because Jiangling's armed forces were abundant and strong, he thereafter harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiangling's armed forces were abundant and strong, he thereafter harbored divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 密書與梁元帝，申其誠款。

translations.literal: He secretly wrote to Emperor Yuan of Liang to express his sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly wrote to Emperor Yuan of Liang to declare his sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 遂有得其書者，進之於詧。

translations.literal: Someone then obtained his letter and presented it to Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Someone then obtained his letter and presented it to Xiao Cha.

sentences.zh: 詧深信佛法，常願不殺誦《法華經》人。

translations.literal: Cha deeply believed in Buddhism and often wished never to kill those who recited the Lotus Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha was a devout Buddhist and often vowed never to kill those who recited the Lotus Sutra.

sentences.zh: 玄成素誦《法華經》，遂以此獲免。

translations.literal: Xuancheng had long recited the Lotus Sutra, and by this he was spared execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng had long recited the Lotus Sutra, and by this he was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 詧後見之，常曰：「甄公好得《法華經》力。」

translations.literal: Later when Cha saw him, he would often say: "Duke Zhen truly gained the power of the 《Lotus Sutra》."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever Xiao Cha saw him, he would remark, "Duke Zhen owes his salvation to the 《Lotus Sutra》.

sentences.zh: 歷位中書侍郎、御史中丞、祠部尚書、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat, Imperial Censor-in-Chief, Director of the Ministry of Rites, and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Vice Director of the Secretariat, Imperial Censor-in-Chief, Director of the Ministry of Rites, and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 詧之六年，卒，贈侍中、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Cha, he died; posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xiao Cha's reign he died and was posthumously granted Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected literary works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected literary works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子詡，少沉敏，閑習政事。

translations.literal: His son Xu was from youth deep and quick-witted and well versed in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu was from youth thoughtful and quick-witted, well versed in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷中書舍人、尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從琮入隋，授開府儀同三司，終於太府少卿。

translations.literal: Following Cong into Sui, he was granted the honors of General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank and ended his life as Vice Director of the Grand Steward's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Xiao Cong into Sui territory, he was granted the honors of General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank and died while serving as Vice Director of the Grand Steward's Office.

sentences.zh: 劉盈，彭城人，以西中郎府錄事參軍隨詧之鎮。

translations.literal: Liu Ying was a native of Pengcheng; he followed Cha to his territorial post as Recording Secretary of the Western Central Commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ying came from Pengcheng and followed Xiao Cha to his territorial post as Recording Secretary of the Western Central Commandery headquarters.

sentences.zh: 有器度，勤於在公。

translations.literal: He had breadth of character and was diligent in public service.
translations.idiomatic: He had breadth of character and was diligent in public service.

sentences.zh: 詧之軍國經謀，頗得參預。

translations.literal: In Cha's military and state planning he participated to a considerable degree.
translations.idiomatic: He participated to a considerable degree in Xiao Cha's military and state planning.

sentences.zh: 歷黃門郎、中書監、雍州刺史、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of the Secretariat, Regional Inspector of Yongzhou, and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of the Secretariat, Regional Inspector of Yongzhou, and Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 巋之七年，卒，贈本官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kui, he died; posthumously granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiao Kui's reign he died and was posthumously granted his former office.

sentences.zh: 第三子然，于時頗知名。

translations.literal: His third son Ran was at the time quite well known.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Ran was at the time quite well known.

sentences.zh: 隋鷹擊郎將。

translations.literal: Under Sui he was Eagle-Strike Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as Eagle-Strike Commandant.

sentences.zh: 岑善方字思義，南陽棘陽人，漢征南大將軍彭之後也。

translations.literal: Cen Shanfang's courtesy name was Siyi; he was a native of Jiyang in Nanyang and a descendant of General Who Conquers the South Peng of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Shanfang, whose courtesy name was Siyi, came from Jiyang in Nanyang and was a descendant of General Who Conquers the South Peng of Han.

sentences.zh: 祖惠甫，給事中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huifu was an Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huifu served as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 父昶，散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Supernumerary Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang served as Supernumerary Cavalry Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 善方有器局，博綜經史，善於辭令。

translations.literal: Shanfang had breadth of capacity, was widely versed in the classics and histories, and was skilled in formal discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Shanfang had breadth of capacity, was widely versed in the classics and histories, and was skilled in formal discourse.

sentences.zh: 以刑獄參軍隨詧至襄陽。

translations.literal: He followed Cha to Xiangyang as Military Adjutant for Criminal Cases.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xiao Cha to Xiangyang as Military Adjutant for Criminal Cases.

sentences.zh: 詧初請內附，以善方兼記室，充使詣闕。

translations.literal: When Cha first sought to submit to the north, Shanfang was made concurrent Chief of Records and sent as envoy to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha first sought to submit to the north, Shanfang was made concurrent Chief of Records and sent as envoy to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 應對閑敏，深為太祖所嘉。

translations.literal: In audience he was easy and quick in response and was deeply praised by the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he was easy and quick in response and was deeply praised by Grand Ancestor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 自此往來，凡數十反。

translations.literal: From then on he traveled back and forth on missions, in all several dozen round trips.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he traveled back and forth on missions, making several dozen round trips in all.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，封長寧縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was granted General of Agile Cavalry, General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changning County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was granted General of Agile Cavalry, General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank, and created Duke of Changning County.

sentences.zh: 詧之承制也，授中書舍人，遷襄陽郡守。

translations.literal: When Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Shanfang was appointed Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and transferred to Administrator of Xiangyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha received provisional appointment as ruler, Shanfang was appointed Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and transferred to Administrator of Xiangyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及稱帝，征為太

translations.literal: When he declared himself emperor, Shanfang was summoned as Director of the Grand
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha declared himself emperor, Shanfang was summoned as Director of the Grand

translations.literal: (the cited text)
translations.idiomatic: (the cited text)

sentences.zh: 〔舟〕卿，領中書舍人，轉太府，領舍人如故。

translations.literal: 〔Fleet〕 Director, concurrently Attendant of the Palace Secretariat; transferred to Minister Steward, keeping the secretariat post as before.
translations.idiomatic: 〔Fleet〕 Director, concurrently Attendant of the Palace Secretariat; he was transferred to Minister Steward while keeping his secretariat post as before.

sentences.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍、起部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Ministry of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Ministry of Construction.

sentences.zh: 善方性清慎，有當世幹能，故詧委以機密。

translations.literal: Shanfang was by nature pure and cautious and possessed the practical ability of the age, and therefore Cha entrusted him with confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shanfang was pure and cautious by nature and possessed the practical ability of the age, and therefore Xiao Cha entrusted him with confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 詧之七年，卒，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Cha, he died; posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiao Cha's reign he died and was posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敬。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Respectful.

sentences.zh: 所著文集十卷。

translations.literal: His collected literary works numbered ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected literary works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有七子，竝有操行。

translations.literal: He had seven sons, all of upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons, all of upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 之元、之利、之象最知名。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan, Zhili, and Zhixiang were the best known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan, Zhili, and Zhixiang were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 之元，太子舍人，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was Attendant to the Crown Prince and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan served as Attendant to the Crown Prince and died young.

sentences.zh: 高祖錄善方充使之功，追之利、之象入朝。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor recorded Shanfang's achievements as envoy and recalled Zhili and Zhixiang to court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu recorded Shanfang's achievements as envoy and summoned Zhili and Zhixiang to court.

sentences.zh: 授之利帥都督、代王記室參軍。

translations.literal: Zhili was granted Commander-in-Chief and Recording Secretary to the Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili was granted Commander-in-Chief and appointed Recording Secretary to the Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 後仕隋，歷安固令、郴義江三州司馬、零陵郡丞。

translations.literal: Later he served Sui, successively holding the posts of Administrator of Angu, Prefectural Marshal of the three prefectures of Chen, Yi, and Jiang, and Assistant Administrator of Lingling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served the Sui, successively as Administrator of Angu, Prefectural Marshal of Chen, Yi, and Jiang, and Assistant Administrator of Lingling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 之象掌式中士，隋文帝相府參軍事。

translations.literal: Zhixiang was Senior Clerk for Ritual Forms and a staff officer in Emperor Wen of Sui's chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang served as Senior Clerk for Ritual Forms and as a staff officer in Emperor Wen of Sui's chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 後仕隋，歷尚書虞部員外郎、邵陵上宜渭南邯鄲四縣令。

translations.literal: Later he served Sui, successively holding the posts of Supernumerary Director in the Ministry of Works of the Imperial Secretariat and Magistrate of the four counties of Shaoling, Shangyi, Weinan, and Handan.
translations.idiomatic: He later served the Sui, successively as Supernumerary Director in the Ministry of Works of the Imperial Secretariat and as magistrate of Shaoling, Shangyi, Weinan, and Handan counties.

sentences.zh: 傅准，北地人。

translations.literal: Fu Zhun was a native of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhun came from Beidi.

sentences.zh: 祖照，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao served as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 父諝，湘東王外兵參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xu was External Military Adjutant to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu served as External Military Adjutant to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 准有文才，善詞賦。

translations.literal: Zhun had literary talent and was skilled at rhapsodies and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun had literary talent and was skilled at rhapsodies and poetry.

sentences.zh: 以西中郎參軍隨詧之鎮。

translations.literal: He followed Cha to his territorial post as Military Adjutant of the Western Central Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xiao Cha to his territorial post as Military Adjutant of the Western Central Commandery.

sentences.zh: 官至度支尚書。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 巋之七年，卒，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kui, he died; posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xiao Kui's reign he died and was posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敬康。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Respectful and Secure.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Respectful and Secure.

sentences.zh: 所著文集二十卷。

translations.literal: His collected literary works numbered twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected literary works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有二子，曰秉曰執，竝材兼文史。

translations.literal: He had two sons, named Bing and Zhi, both talented in both literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Bing and Zhi, both talented in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 秉，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Bing was Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Bing served as Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 執，中書舍人、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Zhi was Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi served as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宗如周，南陽人。

translations.literal: Zong Ruzhou was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ruzhou came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 有才學，容止詳雅。

translations.literal: He had talent and learning, and his bearing and conduct were refined and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: He had talent and learning, and his bearing and conduct were refined and elegant.

sentences.zh: 以府僚隨詧，歷黃門、散騎、列卿，後至度支尚書。

translations.literal: As a staff officer he followed Cha, successively holding the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and various ministers of state, later reaching Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: As a staff officer he followed Xiao Cha, serving successively as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and various ministers of state before rising to Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 巋之九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kui, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xiao Kui's reign he died.

sentences.zh: 如周面狹長，以《法華經》云「聞經隨喜，面不狹長」，嘗戲之曰：「卿何為謗經？」

translations.literal: Ruzhou's face was narrow and long; the 《Lotus Sutra》 says, "Hearing the sutra with joy, one's face is not narrow and long," and Cha once teased him, saying: "Why do you slander the sutra?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhou's face was narrow and long. The 《Lotus Sutra》 says that hearing the sutra with joy keeps one's face from growing narrow and long, so Xiao Cha once teased him: "Why do you slander the sutra?

sentences.zh: 如周踧踖，自陳不謗。

translations.literal: Ruzhou, flustered, declared that he had not slandered it.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhou, flustered, insisted he had not slandered it.

sentences.zh: 詧又謂之如初。

translations.literal: Cha spoke to him again as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Cha spoke to him again as before.

sentences.zh: 如周懼，出告蔡大寶。

translations.literal: Ruzhou, alarmed, went out and told Cai Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Ruzhou went out and told Cai Dabao.

sentences.zh: 大寶知其旨，笑謂之曰：「君當不謗餘經，政應不信《法華》耳。」

translations.literal: Dabao grasped his meaning and said with a smile: "You surely do not slander other sutras—you simply do not believe the 《Lotus Sutra》!"
translations.idiomatic: Dabao grasped his meaning and said with a smile: "You surely do not slander other sutras—you simply do not believe the 《Lotus Sutra》!

sentences.zh: 如周乃悟。

translations.literal: Ruzhou then understood.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhou then understood.

sentences.zh: 又嘗有人訴事於如周，謂為經作如州官也，乃曰：「某有屈滯，故來訴如州官。」

translations.literal: On another occasion someone came to present a grievance to Ruzhou, taking him for the magistrate of Ruzhou because of the sutra pun, and said: "I have a grievance and therefore come to appeal to Magistrate Ruzhou."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion someone came to present a grievance to Ruzhou, mistaking him for the magistrate of Ruzhou because of the earlier pun, and said: "I have a grievance and therefore come to appeal to Magistrate Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 如周曰：「爾何小人，敢呼我名！」

translations.literal: Ruzhou said: "You base fellow—how dare you call out my name!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhou said: "You base fellow—how dare you call out my name!

sentences.zh: 其人慚謝曰：「祇言如州官作如州，不知如州官名如周。

translations.literal: The man apologized in shame: "I meant only to say the magistrate of Ruzhou governs Ruzhou—I did not know the magistrate of Ruzhou is named Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The man apologized in shame: "I meant only to say the magistrate of Ruzhou governs Ruzhou—I did not know the magistrate of Ruzhou is named Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 早知如州官名如周，不敢喚如州官作如周。」

translations.literal: Had I known the magistrate of Ruzhou was named Ruzhou, I would not have dared call the magistrate of Ruzhou "Ruzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Had I known the magistrate of Ruzhou was named Ruzhou, I would not have dared call the magistrate of Ruzhou "Ruzhou."

sentences.zh: 如周乃笑曰：「命卿自責，見侮反深。」

translations.literal: Ruzhou then laughed and said: "I ordered you to blame yourself—yet the insult runs even deeper."
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhou then laughed and said: "I ordered you to blame yourself—yet the insult runs even deeper.

sentences.zh: 衆咸服其寬雅。

translations.literal: All admired his magnanimity and refinement.
translations.idiomatic: All admired his magnanimity and refinement.

sentences.zh: 有七子。

translations.literal: He had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 希顏、希華知名。

translations.literal: Xiyan and Xihua were the best known.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan and Xihua were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 希顏有文學，仕至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Xiyan had literary talent and rose to Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan had literary talent and rose to Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 希華博通經術，為荊楚儒宗。

translations.literal: Xihua was broadly versed in classical learning and was the leading Confucian scholar of Jing-Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Xihua was broadly versed in classical learning and was the leading Confucian scholar of Jing-Chu.

sentences.zh: 蕭欣，梁武帝弟安成康王秀之孫，煬王機之子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Xin was a grandson of Prince Kang of Ancheng, younger brother of Emperor Wu of Liang, and son of Prince Yang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xin was a grandson of Prince Kang of Ancheng, younger brother of Emperor Wu of Liang, and son of Prince Yang Ji.

sentences.zh: 幼聰警，博綜墳籍，善屬文。

translations.literal: From youth he was quick and alert, broadly versed in the classics, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quick and alert, broadly versed in the classics, and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 詧踐位，以欣襲機封。

translations.literal: When Cha ascended the throne, he had Xin inherit Ji's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha ascended the throne, he had Xin inherit Ji's enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、中書令、尚書僕射、尚書令。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 巋之二十三年，卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kui, he died; posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Xiao Kui's reign he died and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 欣與柳信言，當巋之世，俱為一時文宗。

translations.literal: Xin and Liu Xinyan, in Kui's age, were both literary luminaries of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Liu Xinyan were both literary luminaries of Xiao Kui's reign.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又著《梁史》百卷，遭亂失本。

translations.literal: He also authored the 《History of Liang》 in one hundred scrolls, but the original was lost in the disorders.
translations.idiomatic: He also authored the 《History of Liang》 in one hundred scrolls, but the original was lost in the disorders.

sentences.zh: 柳洋，河東解人。

translations.literal: Liu Yang was a native of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yang came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan served as Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父昭，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Zhao was Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洋少有文學，以禮度自拘，與王湜俱以風範方正為當時所重。

translations.literal: Yang from youth had literary talent, restrained himself by ritual propriety, and together with Wang Shi was esteemed by the age for upright bearing and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yang from youth had literary talent and restrained himself by ritual propriety; together with Wang Shi he was esteemed by his contemporaries for upright bearing and conduct.

sentences.zh: 位至吏部尚書，出為上黃郡守。

translations.literal: He rose to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and went out as Administrator of Shanghuang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and was sent out as Administrator of Shanghuang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 梁國廢，以郡歸隋，授開府儀同三司。
