translations.literal: When the Liang state was abolished, he surrendered his commandery to Sui and was granted General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang state was abolished, he surrendered his commandery to the Sui and was granted General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 徐岳，東海人，尚書左僕射、開府儀同三司、簡肅公勉之少子也。

translations.literal: Xu Yue was a native of Donghai and the youngest son of Duke Jiansu Mian, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yue came from Donghai and was the youngest son of Duke Jiansu Mian, Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 少方正，博通經史。

translations.literal: From youth he was upright and square, broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was upright and principled, broadly versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 初為東陽王琮師。

translations.literal: At first he was tutor to Prince Cong of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as tutor to Prince Cong of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 琮為皇太子，授詹事。

translations.literal: When Cong became crown prince, Yue was appointed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong became crown prince, Yue was appointed Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，除侍中、左民尚書，俄遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Yue was appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of the Left Household, and soon transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong succeeded to the throne, Yue was appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of the Left Household, and was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從琮入隋，授上開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Following Cong into Sui, he was granted Senior General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Xiao Cong into Sui territory, he was granted Senior General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 終於陳州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his life as Regional Inspector of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Regional Inspector of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 子凱，秘書郎。

translations.literal: His son Kai was Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai served as Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 岳兄矩，有文學，善吏事。

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother Ju had literary talent and was skilled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's elder brother Ju had literary talent and was skilled in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 頗黷於貨賄。

translations.literal: He was rather tainted by bribery.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather tainted by bribery.

sentences.zh: 位至度支尚書。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of Director of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Director of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子敬，鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His son Jing was Minister Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing served as Minister Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 王漩，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Xuan was a native of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan came from Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 祖琳，侍中、太府卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lin was Palace Attendant and Director of the Grand Steward's Office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lin served as Palace Attendant and Director of the Grand Steward's Office.

sentences.zh: 父錫，侍中。

translations.literal: His father Xi was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 漩少有令譽，尚詧妹廬陵長公主。

translations.literal: Xuan from youth had an excellent reputation; he married Cha's younger sister, the Princess of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan enjoyed an excellent reputation from youth and married Xiao Cha's younger sister, the Princess of Luling.

sentences.zh: 歷秘書郎、太子舍人、宣成王友、廬陵內史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Crown Prince's Household, Companion to the Prince of Xuancheng, and Internal Administrator of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Gentleman of the Secretariat, Attendant of the Crown Prince's Household, Companion to the Prince of Xuancheng, and Internal Administrator of Luling.

sentences.zh: 詧踐位，授侍中、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Cha ascended the throne, he was appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha ascended the throne, he appointed Xuan Palace Attendant and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 巋之四年，使詣闕，卒於賓館。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kui, he was sent as envoy to the imperial court and died in the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kui's reign, he was sent as envoy to the imperial court and died in the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of Palace Attendant and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子瓘，有文詞，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Guan had literary talent and was Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan was a gifted writer who served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 漩弟湜，方雅有器識。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Shi was upright and refined in character and had capacity and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Shi was upright and refined, with capacity and discernment.

sentences.zh: 位至都官尚書。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 巋之二十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kui, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year of Kui's reign.

sentences.zh: 子懷，秘書郎，隋沔陽令。

translations.literal: His son Huai was Secretary Gentleman and, under Sui, Magistrate of Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai served as Secretary Gentleman and, under the Sui, as Magistrate of Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 范迪，順陽人。

translations.literal: Fan Di was a native of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Di was a native of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 祖縝，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen served as Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父胥，鄱陽內史。

translations.literal: His father Xu was Internal Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu served as Internal Administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 迪少機辯，善屬文。

translations.literal: Di from youth was quick and eloquent and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Di was quick-witted and eloquent, and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 歷中書黃門侍郎、尚書右丞、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat, Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat, Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 巋之十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kui, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventeenth year of Kui's reign.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected literary works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected literary works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子裒。

translations.literal: His son Bo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Bo.

sentences.zh: 迪弟遹，文采劣於迪，而經術過之。

translations.literal: Di's younger brother Yu was inferior to Di in literary talent but surpassed him in classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Di's younger brother Yu was less gifted as a writer than Di but surpassed him in classical learning.

sentences.zh: 位至中衛、東平王長史。

translations.literal: He rose to the posts of General of the Central Guard and Chief Administrator to the Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as General of the Central Guard and Chief Administrator to the Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 沈君游，吳興人。

translations.literal: Shen Junyou was a native of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Junyou was a native of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖僧畟，左民尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengji was Director of the Ministry of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengji served as Director of the Ministry of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 父巡，東陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Xun was Grand Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun served as Grand Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 君游博學有詞采，位至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Junyou was broadly learned and had literary gifts; he rose to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Junyou was broadly learned and gifted with literary grace; he rose to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 巋之十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kui, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Kui's reign.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected literary works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected literary works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟君公，有幹局，美風儀，文章典正，特為巋所重。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jungong had practical capacity, fine bearing and appearance, dignified and orthodox literary style, and was especially valued by Kui.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jungong had practical ability, fine bearing, and a dignified literary style, and was especially valued by Xiao Kui.

sentences.zh: 歷中書黃門侍郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat and Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat and Imperial Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 自都官尚書為義興王瓛師。

translations.literal: From the post of Director of the Ministry of Justice he became tutor to Prince Luan of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped down from Director of the Ministry of Justice to become tutor to Prince Luan of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 從瓛奔陳，授侍中、太子詹事。

translations.literal: Following Luan in flight to Chen, he was appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Luan in flight to Chen, he was appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 隋平陳，以瓛同謀度江，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Sui pacified Chen, because Luan had conspired to cross the Yangtze, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui conquered Chen, he was executed for conspiring with Luan to cross the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 袁敞，陳郡人。

translations.literal: Yuan Chang was a native of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chang was a native of Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖昂，司空。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ang was Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ang served as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父士俊，安成內史。

translations.literal: His father Shijun was Internal Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shijun served as Internal Administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 敞少有器量，博涉文史。

translations.literal: Chang from youth had breadth of character and ranged broadly through literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chang had breadth of character and was widely read in literature and history.

sentences.zh: 以吏部郎使詣闕。

translations.literal: As Director of the Ministry of Personnel he was sent as envoy to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: As Director of the Ministry of Personnel, he was sent as envoy to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 時主者以敞班在陳使之後，敞固不從命。

translations.literal: At the time the protocol officer placed Chang's precedence after the Chen envoy's, but Chang firmly refused to obey.
translations.idiomatic: When the protocol officer ranked Chang after the Chen envoy, Chang firmly refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 主者詰之，敞對曰：「昔陳之祖父乃梁諸侯之下吏也，棄忠與義，盜有江東。

translations.literal: The protocol officer questioned him; Chang replied: "In former times Chen's grandfather was but a subordinate official of Liang's feudal lords; he abandoned loyalty and righteousness and stole possession of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol officer questioned him, and Chang replied: "In former times the founder of the Chen house was but a subordinate of Liang's feudal lords; he abandoned loyalty and righteousness and seized Jiangdong by force.

sentences.zh: 今大周朝宗萬國，招攜以禮，若使梁之行人在陳人之後，便恐彝倫失序。

translations.literal: Now Great Zhou receives tribute from the myriad states and summons and embraces them with ritual decorum; if Liang's envoy were placed after the men of Chen, I fear the cardinal norms would fall out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Now Great Zhou receives tribute from all states and draws them in through ritual propriety; if Liang's envoy were ranked after Chen's, I fear the proper order of precedence would be overturned.

sentences.zh: 豈使臣之所望焉。」

translations.literal: How could this be what your minister hoped for?"
translations.idiomatic: Surely this cannot be what your minister would wish."

sentences.zh: 主者不能屈，遂以狀奏。

translations.literal: The protocol officer could not overcome him and therefore submitted a report on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The protocol officer could not sway him and reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖善之，乃詔敞與陳使異日而進。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved and thereupon ordered that Chang and the Chen envoy enter on different days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu approved and ordered that Chang and the Chen envoy be received on separate days.

sentences.zh: 還，以稱旨，遷侍中，轉左民尚書。

translations.literal: Upon his return, because he had fulfilled the imperial intent, he was promoted to Palace Attendant and transferred to Director of the Ministry of the Left Household.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return, having pleased the emperor, he was promoted to Palace Attendant and then transferred to Director of the Ministry of the Left Household.

sentences.zh: 從琮入隋，授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Following Cong into Sui, he was granted General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Xiao Cong into Sui territory, he was granted the honors of General-in-Chief with Pillar of State Protocol of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 終於譙州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his life as Regional Inspector of Qiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Regional Inspector of Qiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 子謐、謙。

translations.literal: His sons Mi and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Mi and Qian.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：梁主任術好謀，知賢養士，蓋有英雄之志，霸王之畧焉。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The lord of Liang was skilled in strategy and fond of planning; he knew the worthy and nurtured scholars — broadly speaking he possessed the ambition of a hero and the strategy of a hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The lord of Liang was skilled in strategy and fond of planning; he recognized talent and nurtured scholars — in short, he possessed heroic ambition and the grand strategy of a true hegemon.

sentences.zh: 及淮海版蕩，骨肉猜貳，擁衆自固，稱藩內款，終能據有全楚，中興頹運。

translations.literal: When the Huai-Hai region was shaken by revolt and kin turned suspicious and divided, he gathered troops to hold himself secure, declared himself a vassal and submitted in good faith, and in the end was able to hold all of Chu and revive a declining fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil swept the Huai-Hai region and kin turned against one another, he rallied his forces, declared vassalage and pledged loyalty to the north, and in the end held all of Chu and revived a declining dynasty.

sentences.zh: 雖土宇殊於舊邦，而位號同於曩日。

translations.literal: Although his territory differed from the old homeland, his titles and rank were the same as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Although his territory was not the old homeland, his titles and imperial rank were unchanged from former days.

sentences.zh: 貽厥自遠，享國數世，可不謂賢哉。

translations.literal: He left a legacy reaching far and enjoyed the state for several generations — can this fail to be called worthy?
translations.idiomatic: He bequeathed a lasting legacy and his dynasty endured for generations — can he fail to be called a worthy ruler?

sentences.zh: 嗣子纂承舊業，增修遺構，賞罰得衷，舉厝有方。

translations.literal: His heir succeeded and carried on the old enterprise, enlarged and repaired what had been left unfinished, kept rewards and punishments balanced, and disposed of affairs with method.
translations.idiomatic: His heir succeeded him and built upon his legacy, enlarging and repairing unfinished works, keeping rewards and punishments even-handed, and governing affairs with skill.

sentences.zh: 密邇寇讐，則威畧具舉；

translations.literal: When closely neighbored by enemy foes, his martial prestige and strategy were fully displayed;
translations.idiomatic: When pressed by neighboring enemies, he displayed full martial prowess and strategic skill;

sentences.zh: 朝宗上國，則聲猷遠振。

translations.literal: when turning toward the superior state in court attendance, his reputation and merit resounded far.
translations.idiomatic: when turning toward the suzerain power, his reputation and achievements resounded far and wide.

sentences.zh: 豈非繼世之令主乎。

translations.literal: Is this not a model ruler who succeeded his generation?
translations.idiomatic: Was he not a model ruler of his generation?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.idiomatic: The full text of this chapter has been collated against the November 1971 Zhonghua Book Company edition of the 《Book of Zhou》.
